When it comes to home decoration, having too much white reminds me of a hospital, and it doesn't feel cozy at all. That's why I prefer warmer, more inviting colors.

part2.cue: Describe an energetic person you know.
points: who this person is, how you know this person
why you consider this person energetic
how you feel about this person
part2.sample:
I'm sure a rare example of someone with seemingly boundless energy is my grandfather. It seems his motto is, "Life's too short to be idle."
Now in his late 70s and retired, he could sleep late, spend more time in bed, read books, or watch TV. But instead, he's always on the go, despite his age. He wakes up with the sun and starts his day with morning exercises outdoors, regardless of the weather or season. Then he gets to work on chores like washing and cleaning. Since my grandmother passed away 20 years ago, he's done all the housework himself. He also works in the yard, the orchard, and his vegetable garden. Yet, he never seems to feel tired. At least, he never says he's tired. In fact, the more he does, the more energized he seems to get. It's incredible. I'm just 30, and I'm nowhere near as active as him. At the end of the day, I can't wait to get home and collapse on the couch. My grandfather, on the other hand, is always up for an evening stroll. I rely on extra-large coffees to get through the day, but he never relies on caffeine. He believes the most powerful source of energy comes from within.
When people ask him how he stays so energized, he always says there are three keys to living a vibrant life.
First, he says his energy levels are directly tied to how refreshed he feels each morning. He never sacrifices sleep, especially for TV, and he eats well. Second, he surrounds himself with the right people - those who are passionate about life, knowledge, and work - and avoids people who constantly complain. Finally, he believes in doing something meaningful with his time. He spreads enthusiasm to everyone around him, and his energy is infectious. I can't help admiring him and wish there were more people like him.

questions: What's the difference between payment for mental work and that for physical work?
Can physical workers receive higher salaries in the future?
What kinds of jobs need a lot of physical work?
Do you think that nowadays all jobs could be done by robots?
Do you think machines could replace human workers in the future?
What are the benefits of replacing human workers with robots?
How have robots and computers changed the way people work?
Why are so many processes controlled by robots instead of people?
samples: These days, mental work is usually paid more than physical work for several reasons. First, people who do mental work, like office jobs, often need special education or skills, which makes their salaries higher. On the other hand, physical work, like construction, doesn't always require formal education, so it's paid less. Second, mental work is often connected to jobs in technology or business, and these fields are in high demand. Because of this, they pay more. Physical jobs, however, are not as popular, so the salaries are usually lower. Finally, some physical jobs can now be done by machines, which means people in those jobs are paid less. But mental work, like creating or managing technology, can't be replaced easily, so it's seen as more valuable and pays more.

Sure. There's a pretty good chance their salaries will go up, if their work remains essential (I mean, if they're not replaced by robots or automation), and at the same time if there's a shortage of workers. This could be the case since nowadays, people are more interested in Al and IT, and fewer want to do physical work. If fewer people want to do physical jobs because they prefer office work or technology, companies might pay more to attract workers.
Plus, as technology improves, some physical jobs might need workers to know how to use new machines or tools.
For example, a worker in a factory might need to learn how to use special robots. This extra knowledge makes the job more important, so the workers might get paid more.

There are a lot of jobs that require physical work. For example, nurses have very demanding jobs. They often need to help patients move, which means they have to lift or support them. They also spend most of their day walking or standing, and they carry medical equipment, which can be quite heavy. Another job that requires a lot of physical work is construction. Construction workers have to carry heavy materials like bricks and wood, use big tools, and sometimes climb up high buildings. They also work outside in all kinds of weather, which makes their job even harder. Finally, farmers also do a lot of physical labor. They spend long hours planting, watering, and harvesting crops. If they take care of animals, they have to carry heavy food and water for them. Farmers often work under the sun or in cold weather, which can be very tiring.

Well, to my mind, the primary benefits of robotization are speed and safety. Unlike human staff, robots don't get distracted or need to take breaks. They also never feel stressed out, and can work all the time, which speeds up production. As far as safety is concerned, robots are a great solution for employers whose human workers have to work at hot temperature or with sharp objects, as machines can easily do tasks of any risk and difficulty level. I'd also add to my list such benefits as consistency as robots never need to divide their attention between a multitude of things and always do just what they are supposed to do... accuracy as robots are programmed for precise, repetitive motion and they are less likely to make mistakes, which means they will always perform tasks with more accuracy than humans... and cost as robots are definitely much cheaper than humans

Did you love stories in your childhood?

And lastly, a story feels more real and engaging when someone reads it aloud. (2) I prefer reading stories. Like to read at my own pace and think deeply about the story. Reading helps me focus and imagine the story in my own way. Plus, I can go back and reread the parts I like, which is easier than finding the same spot when I'm listening.

(3) I prefer reading books because I usually read in bed before I go to sleep. And when I tried listening to audiobooks, I would often fall asleep, and the book would keep playing all night. After that, it was hard to find where I'd left of

questions: Do you like to wear hats?
What kinds of hats do you have?

Why do people wear hats or caps?

samples:
(1) Yes and no. While I hate them in the winter, I can't help loving them the rest of the year. I've got a couple of hats for different purposes. For instance, my favourite one isa wonderful wide-brim hat. What I love is the way it frames my face when I wear it further back on my head. For me, a hat is like a cherry on the cake, it always makes my look more complete than that of non-hatted people. I feel like a star... like Elizabeth Tailor or Angelina Jolie... Sometimes I like wearing hats for practical reasons, you know, as a cover-up for bad-hair days. But in the winter, I hate hats as it's absolutely impossible to take them off without messing up a hairdo.

(2) Not really. Not that I'm timid, but I don't like to be in the centre of everybody's attention, which is inevitable when you're surrounded by non-hatted people wherever you are. So I prefer to go bareheaded.

(1) Well, just my old knitted hat which I wear in the winter to keep my head from cold. And, of course, some cap to prevent a heat stroke in the summer. (1) Like everything I have, I prefer buying hats and caps online First of all, I can find goods at reasonable prices as everyone knows Internet prices are hard to beat. part2.cue: Describe an area of science that interests you.
points: what science is, how you got interested in it
why this science is interesting to you
part2.sample:
Since childhood I've been interested in Astronomy.
Astrophysics, to be precise. This is the branch of Astronomy that studies the physics of stellar phenomena and other objects in space. Though I have to admit that I'm not a science-obsessed person. I mean, if I come across an interesting article, I read it with pleasure. If I don't, I don't deliberately search for this information, nor do I do it regularly. From time to time I watch documentaries, read articles on the Internet, get some new information from friends. But as I've said before, I don't do it very often. I don't really remember what got me into space and all that stuff. It feels like I've been interested in it for as long as I can remember. For example, by the time I was five, I already recall being interested in Astronomy. I think I got started on the science track when I started reading a lot of science fiction books and encyclopedias as a child. Also, my parents read me books on planets and my father told me many interesting facts about our solar system. My interest to this topic was fueled several years ago after watching Interstellar, a wonderful science fiction movie which made me think about black holes, wormholes, space time, dark matter, time dilation for several weeks. I was more than impressed.
The main reason why I like Astrophysics is that everything mysterious captivates me. I really want to understand how everything that exists works, to have a better understanding of the universe we live in and understand how the cosmos influences different processes on our planet.

questions: Should scientists explain the research process to the public?
Should people continue studying science after finishing school?
How do you find out about scientific news?
Why do some children not like learning science at school?
Do you think science is important?
How does science influence our life?
Should children learn science?
What science subject is the most important for children to learn?
samples:
I think it would be good if they did so. First of all, transparency would play a significant role in demystifying scientific practices, dispelling misconceptions, and building a stronger relationship between scientists and the public.
For example, when climate scientists explain their methodologies for collecting data and running simulations, it helps the public understand the severity of climate change and the urgency of action. In addition, sharing the research process can inspire the younger generation to pursue careers in science and research. Finally, public dissemination of the research process helps in dispelling skepticism surrounding scientific findings. For example, when vaccine researchers explain the rigorous testing procedures and safety evaluations, it can address concerns and build confidence in the efficacy and safety of vaccines.

Yes, I think studying science is super important not only for people who want to be scientists because, first of all, everyone can use this knowledge in their daily life. For example, studying biology teaches us how to take care of our health, and chemistry helps us understand what things like food or medicine are made of. Also, science teaches logical thinking. I mean, when we study science, we learn how to find answers, check facts, and solve problems.
These skills are important for any job. Finally, it helps us understand what's going on in the world. For example, it explains things like why the climate is changing or how new technology works. This is useful because it helps people find solutions to big problems, like saving energy or fighting diseases.

I mostly find out about scientific news on Instagram, YouTube, and TikTok. On Instagram, I follow pages like Science Daily where they post cool facts, like how scientists are working on new ways to recycle plastic. On YouTube, I watch videos from science channels that explain stuff like why the sky is blue or how robots are being used in space.
And on TikTok, there are short videos of scientists doing fun experiments, like making colorful reactions or showing how gravity works with simple tricks.

Some children may not enjoy learning science at school due to various reasons. Firstly, they might have a hard time relating scientific concepts to their daily lives, making it seem abstract and uninteresting. Additionally, the teaching methods used in some schools, often relying on lectures and textbooks, can make science classes appear dull. Fear of making mistakes can also be a factor, as science involves experimentation and problem-solving.
Furthermore, the complexity of scientific theories and terminology can be intimidating, especially for younger students. Limited hands-on experiences and inadequate resources in schools may hinder their engagement. Gender stereotypes, which can discourage girls from pursuing science, are another concern. In some cases, negative past experiences or a lack of exposure to science-related careers may contribute to a child's disinterest.

Oh, I would even say it's of primary importance 'cause it pushes back the boundaries constraining our knowledge and provides the potential for long-term benefit worldwide. Science defines us, our world and our universe. It is the engine of prosperity, the system of exploring and innovation. Science lets us make progress as a race allowing us to protect ourselves from the environment and the environment from our impact. So, to sum up, it is very important and even vital.

I believe that Biology is a fundamental science subject that children should prioritize in their education. Firstly, Biology helps youngsters understand the complexities of life itself, including human anatomy, ecosystems, and the diversity of species on Earth. This knowledge is not only fascinating but also essential for making informed decisions about health and environmental conservation. Furthermore, by studying Biology, children can develop critical thinking skills as they learn about biological processes and the impact of factors like pollution and climate change on living organisms. Moreover, Biology has numerous real-world applications.
For instance, it's the foundation for medical and healthcare professions, which play a vital role in society. Additionally, Biology underpins advancements in biotechnology, such as genetic engineering and pharmaceutical research.
Therefore, a strong foundation in Biology equips children with valuable skills and knowledge that can lead to rewarding careers and contribute to solving global challenges like disease outbreaks and environmental sustainability.

Well, people in my country really like to give books and handmade gifts as well as home décor presents such as frames, figurines and candles. All these things create comfort and remind the receiver of the giver's love and affection. Many people also give flowers and chocolates, especially as "Thank you" presents and cash as a birthday or wedding gift.

Oh no, I don't. Expensive gifts mean more pressure on my monthly expense, which, in turn, means I will have to refuse from something I really need in order to please another person with something costly. What is more, I don't want to buy anybody's love with material things. I'd better do it with actions.
Oh, I actually do it quite often. I would even say almost every day. Just because I like to show thoughtfulness, love and affection to close people and raise a smile on their faces.

I guess there are a lot of reasons why people do it. For example, to show interest and appreciation, or express gratitude to others. People also give gifts to mark milestones and just bring joy and pleasure to the ones they love.

Oh yeah, it happened to me a while ago. I got a key box from my mate which I didn't like at all as it was big and heavy enough and I just couldn't come up with an idea when and where to use it. And still, I struggled to bring a smile to my face to show gratitude to the giver as any present,/u>, to my mind, is worth a 'thank you'.

My sink is always empty and clean - there are never dirty dishes in it. And what's important is that everything has a place and is in the place it belongs. I'd say my home is clean enough for guests to visit unexpectedly.

(2) It's super clean. I clean my house on a regular basis to maintain a healthy living environment 'cause dust is a very common cause for colds, coughs, asthma attacks, breathing and respiratory problems, and various types of allergies. Plus, Ilike when it's clean enough to be prepared for surprise visitors.

(3) Oh, my house is constantly messy no matter how hard I try to keep it clean. The thing is that I have a cat. So everything is covered with my cat's hair, so much that it's like a snowstorm in my house. And I'm constantly finding fur everywhere. No matter how often I vacuum it just keeps coming back. It's like a never-ending battle.

(4) I wish it were, but I just don't have time for a cleaning routine. I work full time, and in the evenings I feel so tired that cleaning is what I want to do least. Plus, I have two kids, and they are messmakers. They throw toys around, play with their arts and crafts materials on the floor, and run around like crazy.

(1) What I hate is vacuuming! I think it's because of the noise and monotonous nature of pushing a vacuum around. It just gets on my nerves and bores me to death. Another reason why I hate doing this chore is that I don't like having to move furniture and reach into all the far corners of my house. Plus, every time I vacuum, dust and pet dander get stirred up into the air and make me sneeze and itch. So it's not only a chore that I dread, but it also causes me physical discomfort.

(2) The chore I hate is washing the dishes. It's one of those things that needs to be done every single day, and it's a big pain 'cause I have a lot of pots and pans to clean. Plus, it takes so long because I have to scrub each dish separately. What makes it worse for me is that my hands are always so dry after I finish. But I just can't get used to using gloves.

(3) What I really hate is doing the dishes. So I just say to myself that I will do them tomorrow and just let them pile up. But as you know 'tomorrow never comes'. And the longer I procrastinate, the harder it is to make myself do the chore.
As a result, every day, they slowly accumulate... Lots of plates covered in sauces and crumbs, bowls with a layer of sticky who-knows-what, forks, knives, and spoons all gummed with bits of this and that.

(1) It may sound weird, but I love washing the dishes. It's one of my favorite chores! First of all, doing repetitive motions is calming. I would even say it's therapeutic to me. And I normally use this time to practice mindfulness. I mean, I try to focus on the task at hand, and it helps me clear my mind and relax. Plus, I enjoy listening to the soft sounds of the water running and the gentle clinking of dishes against each other as I wash them. It's like a mini-meditation session for me.

(2) My favourite chore is washing the dishes. First of all, it's a great way to show my family how much I care about them and our home. Plus, when it's all done, I get that feeling of accomplishment and satisfaction when I look at sparkling clean dishes in a freshly wiped sink. And it can be fun. Sometimes I sing along to my favorite songs while washing the dishes and it makes the chore seem less tedious. Sometimes I listen to podcasts and audiobooks. So it can be educational as well.

Plus, it can save me quite a bit of money 'cause home-cooked meals can be a lot cheaper than buying food at restaurants or getting take out.

(2) Well, cooking is not my thing 'cause it takes too much time and effort. I mean, why bother when there are so many delicious options out there? Stores are filled with readymade meals that are just as tasty. And I can go to a cafe or restaurant whenever I want to. Plus, I don't think I have the patience or skill to cook complicated dishes. And it's not like it's necessary for survival or anything. There are just too many other things that I'd rather do with my time.

Oh yes, I adore it. Cooking at home is always a fun time with my family 'cause we like to cook together. It also lets me control my family's health. What's more, it lets me save money as I have a choice about where and how many products to buy. One more thing I can add is that homemade food tastes much better, especially when I see happy faces of my beloved ones enjoying the meal.

Well, I am the one who always cooks in my home. I do it because I adore cooking and because I am really good at it.
I can easily make a great meal out of random fridge ingredients, and it makes life easy for all my family members. One more reason why I cook for everyone is the fact that I have enough time for that. Though, from time to time my husband and kids help me in the kitchen but not more often than once a week, to my regret.

part2.cue: Describe an occasion when the vehicle you took broke down in your travel.
points: where you were going, who was with you
whether it took long to repair it
part2.sample:
In my experience, things go wrong when I least expect it. Last winter, I had an overnight bus journey from Big City to Cool City.
When I found out I needed to make this trip, train tickets were already sold out, and buying a plane ticket was out of the question. It was way too expensive. So, taking the bus was my only option at the time.
I hate travelling long distances by bus, especially at night, mostly because I can't sleep sitting up. This was exactly the case. Since I couldn't sleep, I stared out of the window. It was almost dawn, so I could barely see anything, but it was still better than staring at the back of the seat in front of me.
Suddenly I heard a dull thud, and a few minutes later, the bus stopped. The driver got off to check, but he didn't come back for half an hour.
At first, everything seemed ok. All the passengers were sleeping and had no idea something was wrong. If I had been able to sleep, I probably wouldn't have noticed anything either. But unfortunately, I wasn't as lucky as the others.
Several hours later everyone woke up and realized that we were stuck in the middle of nowhere. The worst part? There was no toilet - not even trees or bushes in sight. Just an endless field. For people like me, who are used to modern conveniences, it was a nightmare.
As time went on, people grew angrier by the hour. Some passengers even lost their temper and started yelling at the driver, even though it wasn't his fault. He was doing everything he could to fix the problem, but it wasn't easy.
We ended up spending five or six hours on the side of the highway before we could finally continue the journey. But I wasn't really happy because I missed a very important meeting.

part2.topic: Place in the village you visited
part2.cue: Describe a place in the village you visited.
part2.sample:
Last Sunday, I went to the village to visit my grandparents.
During the pandemic, I didn't visit them at all because I was afraid to infect them. I missed them very much. My grandpa even said he was more afraid to die of loneliness than of coronavirus. So since the pandemic, I've been visiting them more often to make up for the time we lost even though it takes me 5 hours to get there.
My grandparents live in a quiet and beautiful place by the river. They have a cozy house with a big garden. There are lots of flowers, and sometimes orchids bloom too. You know, being there is like travelling back in time. Everything reminds me of my carefree childhood: my toys, old CDs, my bicycle. It feels like you step into another world. All the walls are still covered with old wallpaper. My grandmother doesn't allow us to remove it, and she refuses to get their house refurbished because she wants to keep all their memories alive. She says they both love their 50-year-old chairs and armchairs, their old wooden table in the kitchen, paintings, clay pots, old pictures, and lots of things they bought when they were young.
You know, I think she's right. There's something special about this old house. It's a magical place, and I really love spending time there. When I visit, I enjoy going fishing and exploring the countryside during the day. In the evenings, I watch the sunset from the backyard. I drink hot tea and eat cinnamon buns. My grandmother always bakes them when I come because she knows how much I love them. If I didn't have so much on my plate and if the trip didn't take so long, I would visit them more often.

part2.sample:
My grandfather was a doctor. He had been working at a regional hospital for more than 50 years until he retired.
He started his career as a doctor's assistant, and later became a doctor. He examined, diagnosed and treated patients. He literally worked day and night. I think it was hard. Very hard. But I'm sure that he did exactly what he was born to do, and he wouldn't have changed his job for all the world. For him, it wasn't just a job, it was his calling. My grandfather's work occupied all his time. He never had a second job. It was just impossible as he had no time for that. If he had had a second job, he would have died of fatigue. Sometimes I doubted my grandfather was a human being. He didn't have hobbies. He didn't spend time with friends. He even missed most family gatherings. You know, it's not fun at all. He was always tired, and his eyes were always red because of endless sleepless nights. When he wasn't on duty, he was reading different books and reviewing medical records of his patients.
In my opinion, it is a very rewarding job. But I wouldn't like to do anything like that because it's really stressful, especially when you understand that you cannot help some patient. Plus, shift work is not my thing. I can't imagine myself working night shifts. What's more, I don't want to sacrifice everything for work.

part2.topic: Positive change in your daily routine
part2.cue: Describe a positive change that you have made recently in your daily routine.
points: what the change is and how you've made it
why you think it's a positive change
how you feel about the change
part2.sample:
About six months ago, I read this book called The Miracle Morning. It really inspired me to try waking up at 5 a.m.
At first, it was insanely hard because I was the type of person who would stay in bed as long as possible, hitting snooze like five times. But little by little, it got easier. Finally, I got used to waking up early. And now I wake up at 5 a.m. without any struggle. Honestly, it's been a game-changer for me. Before, I used to wake up already feeling tired, like I'd been carrying heavy loads all night. I'd feel drained all day long. I used to drink three cups of coffee just to function. And even that didn't always help. I have no idea how it works, but now I feel full of energy.
This change has made me so much more productive, both at work and at home. Plus, I finally have time for myself. In the mornings, while everyone else is still asleep, I read, do yoga, meditate, and plan my day. Sometimes, I watch interesting YouTube videos or listen to podcasts. So I can see how much my life has improved because of this simple habit.

samples: Oh, I am sure it is. Unfortunately, time is limited, there are only 24 hours in a day and no one can store or save time for later use. Efficient time management will help you to accomplish more with less effort and eliminate the pressure that comes from feeling like you don't have enough time. It will also put you in line for advancement opportunities improving your decision-making ability and helping make conscious choices, which will let you become more successful in your studies and career. So, no doubt, effective time management is very important.

Everything depends on what you mean by 'frequently'.
Changing companies as often as every two to five years is definitely an accepted pace in today's marketplace whereas job-hopping is still seen as something negative 'cause people who move jobs frequently are perceived by most employers as inconsistent and lacking in commitment.
Although I must admit, it's much more acceptable than in the past. Research has found that employees who stay in the same job for more than two years will earn 50 percent less over their lifetime than people who change companies more frequently. So despite the fact that job-hoppers are regarded as somewhat unreliable workers, they receive more money than those who are loyal to a company they work for. Plus, it helps people shift their career paths toward their interests and values 'cause exploring the job market helps them understand more quickly what exactly they are looking for.

questions: How do we choose gifts?

Why do people give gifts?

samples: When picking gifts for friends or family, we typically begin by thinking about what they like. For example, if the recipient is into gardening, we might look for a nice plant or gardening tools. It's all about finding something that resonates with their hobbies and preferences.

Well, people in my country really like to give books and handmade gifts as well as home décor presents such as frames, figurines and candles. All these things create comfort and remind the receiver of the giver's love and affection. Many people also give flowers and chocolates, especially as "Thank you" presents and cash as a birthday or wedding gift.

Oh no, I don't. Expensive gifts mean more pressure on my monthly expense, which, in turn, means I will have to refuse from something I really need in order to please another person with something costly. What is more, I don't want to buy anybody's love with material things. I'd better do it with actions.
Oh, I actually do it quite often. I would even say almost every day. Just because I like to show thoughtfulness, love and affection to close people and raise a smile on their faces.

I guess there are a lot of reasons why people do it. For example, to show interest and appreciation, or express gratitude to others. People also give gifts to mark milestones and just bring joy and pleasure to the ones they love.

(1) It may sound weird, but I love washing the dishes. It's one of my favorite chores! First of all, doing repetitive motions is calming. I would even say it's therapeutic to me. Sometimes I sing along to my favorite songs while washing the dishes and it makes the chore seem less tedious. Sometimes I listen to podcasts and audiobooks. So it can be educational as well.

And I can use this time to focus on my thoughts and feelings without any distractions from other people or technology

No, I don't always have breakfast at home. Sometimes I'm in a rush and I'll grab something quick on the go, like a granola bar or a piece of fruit. (1) Yeah, I'd love to. If I learn to cook like a pro, I will be able to experiment with different flavors, ingredients, and cooking techniques to create dishes that are truly unique and tailored specifically towards my tastes and preferences.

Well, I am the one who always cooks in my home. I do it because I adore cooking and because I am really good at it.

One more reason why I cook for everyone is the fact that I have enough time for that. points: what it is, when you bought it
part2.sample:

That's exactly what happened with a pair of sneakers I bought a few weeks ago. I bought them because I saw a big discount online and thought, 'Wow, such a great deal!' I placed the order right away, without second-guessing. When I tried them on at home, they seemed perfect. They looked amazing and felt fine. I couldn't wait to wear them out. So I decided to take them for a walk the very next day.
When I started walking, I felt something was off, but at that point, I couldn't figure out what exactly was wrong. The next day, I gave them another shot. I was hoping they'd get better with time. But they didn't. This time, it hurt everywhere, and my left foot was literally one big blister.
The sneakers were beautiful and high-quality, but I knew I'd never wear them again. So I had no choice but to return them.

part2.cue: Describe an occasion when you forgot something important.
points: what you forgot, why you forgot it
part2.sample:
This mishap happened to me a long time ago, but I still remember it like it was yesterday. My boss invited me to lunch to discuss my long-term career plans. I had even heard through the grapevine that he was going to offer me a new position and a bigger project.
One day, when I was supposed to be at the café, I was in the office working as if everything was normal. It wasn't until I saw my boss's name on my phone screen that I remembered our meeting.
You know, I was absolutely shocked. I had a panic attack, and I just wanted the ground to open up and swallow me. I couldn't believe I had completely forgotten about it. It just slipped my mind.
I realized how awful the situation was. My boss had rearranged his busy schedule to meet me, and I hadn't even shown up. I felt deeply ashamed of what had happened, and I didn't have a single excuse. I felt so guilty knowing he had wasted his valuable time waiting for me instead of focusing on something important. I was terrified that he might think I didn't value the opportunity or respect his time.
On top of that, I was in shock because nothing like this had ever happened to me before, and I didn't know how to handle it. Of course, I apologized a hundred times, but it didn't make me feel any better. I knew he had wasted his precious time because of me, and I couldn't forgive myself for it.

These are the most common things, I guess.

Well, I guess it may be so for a score of reasons. If not to consider age-related memory loss and memory-impairing illnesses such as Alzheimer's disease but focus on memory problems typical for healthy people, I think that one of the most common reasons for forgetfulness is that people are just absentminded and don't pay close enough attention to the things that happen to them. One more reason I can name is emotional disorders such as stress, anxiety or depression and, as a result, sleep disorders that make people take certain medications which can cause forgetfulness and confusion. What else? Well, this may happen because of some kind of vitamin deficiency and, of course, because of a lack of storage space in the brain as brains of some people are overloaded with tons of information.

Oh, there are many fun, simple and even, I'd say, delicious ways to improve memory. First of all, it's necessary to eat a brain-boosting diet because the brain needs fuel just as much as the body does. What I consider healthy for the brain is lots of fruits and vegetables, whole grains, lean protein and healthy fats such as olive oil, nuts, fish and fish oil supplements. For brain health, though, it's not just what we eat but also what we don't eat matters. So, in order to boost the brain power and memory we should eat less added sugar and cut down on refined carbs such as cakes, cereal, cookies and white bread. Secondly, in order to help our brain and memory stay sharp we should exercise more as physical activity increases oxygen to the brain and reduces the risk for disorders that lead to memory loss.
One more important thing for improving the memory is playing different brain games like crosswords, word-recall games and even mobile app games dedicated to memory training as memory, like muscular strength, requires us to use it or lose it. Well, and of course we should consider such things as getting enough sleep, taking breaks throughout the day, using different tricks such as visualisation while memorising something and setting a healthy balance between work and leisure time as only a combination of all these methods can give us really good results.

Oh, I think that they are very responsible and disciplined, first of all. Also, I think that they know their goals and like to be sure that they are staying on track with them. One more thing I can say about them is that they don't like to waste their time, and use calendars in order to produce quality work without taking unnecessary, unfocused and inefficient steps.

what happens if someone breaks it
part2.sample:
So, at my work, there's this one rule that everyone knows about, and it's all about being on time. It's a pretty simple rule, really. But it's super important for keeping things running smoothly. I mean we work in a busy office where we have to coordinate a lot of tasks and projects. If someone is late, it can mess up the whole schedule. Meetings get delayed, deadlines get pushed back, and it can be a real headache for everyone. So if it weren't for this rule, we would have a really hard time getting work done. Literally. So, I totally get why this rule is in place, and I actually think it's a good one. It helps us stay organized and make sure we're all on the same page. Plus, it shows respect for our colleagues and the company because we're valuing everyone's time.
But here's the thing: not everyone followed this rule. There were a few coworkers who were constantly late, and it was frustrating. It was not fair to the rest of us who made an effort to be on time, and it often created tension in the office.
Now, if someone does break this rule and is late without a good reason, there are consequences. Usually, our boss will have a chat with them and remind them of the importance of being punctual. If it keeps happening, they might get a formal warning. And if it continues after that, well, they could even lose their job.
So, while the rule about being on time might seem strict, I think it's necessary to keep things running smoothly and maintain a respectful work environment. And personally, I'm all for it because it makes my workday a lot less stressful.

part2.cue: Describe an important decision that you once made.
points: what the decision was, how you made your decision
what the results of the decision were
why it was difficult to make
part2.sample:
A few years ago, I made a decision that completely changed my life. I had been working at the same company for nearly 5 years. It was a stable job with a steady income, but deep down I knew I wasn't happy. I felt like I was stuck in a rut and there were no opportunities to grow professionally or be promoted. I had always dreamed of starting my own business, but the idea of leaving my stable job and taking such a big risk was terrifying. However, as time went on, 1 became more and more unhappy with my current situation.
I began to realize that if I didn't make a change soon, I might regret it for the rest of my life.
I started doing research, talking to other entrepreneurs, and developing a business plan. I also spoke to my friends and family about my decision and sought their support. It wasn't an easy decision to leave my stable job, but I knew it was the right one. I was nervous about the financial risk and the potential for failure, but I also felt excited about the prospect of pursuing my dream and creating something that was truly my own. It's been a few years since I started my business, and it hasn't always been easy. There have been many ups and downs, but I have never regretted my decision to take the leap. I feel fulfilled and challenged in a way that I never did in my previous job, and I know that I made the right choice for myself and my future.

questions: Do you think advertisements can influence our decisions when shopping?
What important decisions do young people need to make after the completion of high school?
Do you think the influence of advertising is good?
How do people make important decisions?
Who can children turn to for help when making a decision?

samples: Absolutely. Nowadays there are lots of marketing tools and tactics that can affect consumer behaviour and decisions, and therefore make customers choose particular goods or services. First of all, companies launch marketing campaigns that cause consumers to react to them. The more people react to your marketing campaigns, the more they will talk about them the more they discuss your brand and products, the more likely people are to buy them. As a result, companies spend inordinate amounts of money on advertising, especially on social media. To make ads effective and form a deep connection with the audience, marketers create messages that tap into human emotion and everyone's desire to be happy. Sometimes they try to highlight the scarcity of the offer to create a sense of urgency, for example, by using limited-time offer ads. Companies offer free samples, generous discounts, free shipping and other promotional deals to gain an edge over the competition. They use various techniques to make customers feel like they're getting more than what they're paying for, for example, by using the "buy one, get one free" strategy. Also, to increase visibility and attractiveness of products, marketers use packaging and labeling. Finally, a lot of brands today form communities, both online and offline, where their loyal customers share common interests together because the need to belong is one of our most basic needs that motivate our behavior. So, as you see, there are lots of ways to make customers buy specific products and buy more of them.

After graduation, teenagers are faced with several important decisions that will shape their future. One of the most crucial decisions is choosing a career path. It's essential to consider their skills, interests, and goals when making this decision, as it can have a significant impact on their future. They need to research different career options, speak to people in those fields, and assess whether they would enjoy and excel in that career. The decision to choose a career path will then have an impact on the next significant decision teenagers need to make after graduation, which is deciding on further education. If they have decided on a specific career path, they need to research the education requirements for that field and choose the appropriate educational path to pursue. If they plan to attend college or university, they will need to select a major or field of study that aligns with their career goals.
This decision will have an impact on the courses they take, the skills they develop, and their future career opportunities. Another important decision is whether to move out or continue living at home. Some teenagers may choose to move out and live independently, while others may prefer to stay with their parents. Moving out means taking on responsibilities such as paying rent, bills, and other living expenses. On the other hand, staying at home can provide a sense of security and financial stability, but it can also limit their independence. Finally, after graduation, teenagers need to start managing their finances. This includes paying bills, saving money, and managing debt. They need to learn how to create and stick to a budget, as well as how to save money for the future. This decision is crucial for their financial well-being and can have long-term effects on their future financial stability.

Advertising is a crucial component of any successful business strategy. It allows companies to make themselves more visible and accessible to a wide range of potential customers. By highlighting their business beyond their local area and reaching out to their target audience worldwide, companies can expand their customer base and increase their revenue. One of the key benefits of advertising is its ability to target a very specific segment of people. This allows companies to find the right audience for their products or services, which further helps them in generating more leads and making their campaigns more effective and profitable. Additionally, advertising helps companies keep their target audience engaged by providing them with relevant and useful information about the company and its offerings. Another benefit of advertising is its ability to help companies reach their goals quickly. The moment a company starts its ad campaign, it can start receiving qualified leads, which can lead to increased sales and revenue. Overall, advertising is an essential tool for any business looking to grow and succeed in today's competitive marketplace.

When faced with the need to make an important decision, people often begin by actively seeking out and collecting relevant information from various sources. People actively seek out and collect relevant information from various sources. They conduct research, read extensively, consult experts, and explore different avenues to ensure they have the necessary knowledge before reaching a conclusion. For example, when faced with choosing a career path, individuals often delve into researching job prospects, the skills required in different fields, and the prevailing trends within the industry. Also, people frequently rely on weighing the pros and cons of different options. So people can effectively evaluate the potential outcomes and select the option that aligns best with their goals and priorities. For example, when deciding between two job offers, someone might think about things like how much they'll get paid, how well they can balance work and personal life, the chances for growth, and the atmosphere at the company. This helps them pick the job that has the best overall benefits for them.

Children can turn to many people for help when making a decision. First, they can ask their parents or guardians because these adults know them well and want the best for them. For example, if a child feels nervous about joining a new sports team, they might ask their parents if they should try it and how to handle their fear. Second, children can turn to teachers for school-related decisions. For instance, if a child feels bullied, a teacher can help resolve the problem. Or if they're having a hard time understanding a science topic, they can ask their teacher to explain it more clearly. Friends or older siblings can also help with smaller decisions, like choosing clothes or toys. Finally, in emergencies, children might ask other trusted adults, such as a neighbor or a store employee, for guidance.

Yes, there are many occasions when a child has to make decisions that can affect their safety (or even their life), their self-esteem, confidence, or relationships with others. For example, sometimes when a child is lost and there are no adults to help them, they might have to choose whether to ask a stranger for help, look for a police officer, or go into a big store to find someone safe. Children also have to make important decisions when they have a problem or conflict at school. In such situations, they need to decide whether to tell their parents and ask for help or try to solve the problem by themselves. Sometimes, they have to choose how to spend their money. For example, they might need to decide whether to buy a toy, save it, or spend it on something useful. And there are plenty of other situations like this when children have to make what feels like a life-changing decision on their own.

part2.cue: Describe a foreign country you'd like to visit in the future.
points: what it is, where it is
part2.sample:

I started surfing the internet, reading travel blogs, and watching videos on YouTube. One of the countries I came across was Cuba. I saw lots of pictures of its remarkable mountains, spectacular limestone hills, vast tobacco plantations, butter-soft beaches, lush green countryside, and colorful colonial cities. At some point, I realized there was something about Cuba that made me put it at the very top of my travel wish list. Many travellers say that it's a truly unique place. The thing is, the country was isolated from the rest of the world for many years. And despite the fact that most restrictions were lifted some years ago, it hasn't changed a lot since then. Everyone says it seems to be lost in time, somewhere in the 1950's. I mean, people usually describe it as a place with salsa and rumba music playing everywhere, men smoking cigars and drinking rum, old American cars in the streets, and the beautiful colonial buildings with peeling paint in Old Havana. For me, it's really hard to believe that anything like that is possible in our modern world. So I want to experience it for myself.
At the moment, I don't know more than that, and I'm not planning to continue my research 'cause if I learn everything before visiting, there will be nothing left to discover when I go there one day. It won't be interesting. I know myself. So I really want to know more about this country, but I don't want to explore it from my couch.

questions: Do you think it's important to have a national identity?

What makes one country different from the other?

What is the best way to learn a foreign culture?

samples:
Absolutely. A national identity is what unites all citizens into one nation. It builds a strong bond among all members of the society. So, first of all, it plays a key role in creating and maintaining a democracy and political order in society.
What's more, a national identity is the basis of national security. I mean when people feel they belong in a particular society, they feel as a part of this group, they are less likely to break the law or hurt others in any way. Another reason why a national identity matters is that a common identity defines citizens' membership in a country and places them in relation to other persons who are also citizens, or other persons from other countries. Also, a national identity plays a key role in determining whether people view immigration as a threat - those who identify with their country are more negative toward immigration. Finally, having a national identity is key to preserving the cultural heritage of a nation. I mean people are eager to speak their native language, follow their nation's customs and traditions, study the nation's history, and respect everything that represents the values of the nation.

Well, national identity is essentially socially constructed and the process of acquisition of this complex system of knowledge, beliefs and feelings takes place over a period of many years spanning both childhood and adolescence.
Social identity can arise as a direct result of the presence in people's daily lives of such elements as national symbols, language, the nation's history, national consciousness, and cultural artifacts. To put it simply, people should learn about their nation's flag and national colours. They should study the history of their nation as well as the history of their national consciousness. People can cook their national dishes, speak their native language, listen to traditional music, visit museums and art galleries, watch local films, and follow their nation's traditions and customs. Another important thing that is intrinsically linked to national identity is values. So what people should and can do is adopt beliefs, values, assumptions and expectations which align with those shared by a group of people they belong to.

Oh, I think that one of the main advantages of working for a multinational company is growth and job opportunities from assisting with translation needs during a conference call at the home office to travelling to an out-of-the-country office and assisting with any company needs there. Well, and of course, business trips to international and domestic offices of the company, and a chance to experience other cultures and gain diversity in the workplace. As far as the drawbacks are concerned, I'd name time zones because of the need to prepare work duties for the day in a timely manner for out-of-country coworkers or the need to be available for conference calls and business meetings at all hours of the night. Lastly, I can't help mentioning frequent job conflicts based on cultural differences.

Well, travelling is wonderful in many ways, and there are a lot of benefits people can have from it. First of all, travelling lets people disconnect from their regular life, relax and get new experiences. It also helps them open their eyes to how the rest of the world lives and, as a result, gain a broader worldview. While travelling, people get to know different places, get accustomed to different cultures, increase their general knowledge and make friends from all over the globe. All these things and experiences make them inspired and happy and create memories for a lifetime.

Oh, I guess its territory, population and government, first of all. I would also add its history as well as customs and traditions to this list. Oh, and its laws, climate and nature too. At least this is what makes one country different from the other for me.

Well, I can't say that it's the best way to immerse in a foreign culture for everyone, but it's definitely one of the best ways for the majority of people I know as reading exposes us to the culture giving us a chance to learn about etiquette, values, festivals and religion. What is more, books written by locals give us a glimpse into the mind and life of the people from that culture helping us to learn a lot about their mentality. Oh, and one more important thing.
Culture consists of patterns, both explicit and implicit, and books often conceal the culture's quirks in the details. So yeah, reading is definitely not the worst way to know about a new culture, I guess.

Well, I don't think there is just one way to learn a foreign culture. I'd rather say that it's a combination of ways that helps people immerse themselves in another culture and learn as much as possible about it. The way the majority of people usually opt for is travelling or moving to the country with the culture they want to experience in order to live among people who represent that culture and learn about things such as their values, cuisine, and fashion. But I think that people who can't afford to travel still have a great chance to get acquainted with the culture they are interested in by reading travel books, travel journals and guides to get information about etiquette, gender roles, festivals, and religion. If people don't like reading, they can look up YouTube videos dedicated to a specific culture or aspects of a culture, or get a pen or email pal to ask them all those questions they need answers to.

part2.cue: Describe a time you made a promise to someone.
points: whether it was easy or difficult to keep
part2.sample:
When I was a child, I really wanted to have a dog. But my parents didn't seem to be charmed by the idea 'cause when I said 'dog', I imagined playing with my puppy, petting him, sleeping side by side at night, whereas my parents must have heard 'time, expenses, a lot of extra work, and possible destruction of furniture and household goods'. So no matter how much I begged, they just kept saying 'no'!
But I wanted to have a dog so desperately that I decided to go to extremes and promise my parents to take care of the dog and clean my room. So, one day, they said 'yes'. At first, I was really excited, so I did all my household tasks without being nagged to do so. I made my bed, cleaned my room almost every day, took out the trash, and did the dishes. I walked the dog twice a day, fed him, and cleaned up any accidents he had in the flat. But my excitement faded really quickly 'cause I underestimated what this would take. I mean having a dog is like having a baby. You just can't wake up early to walk the dog one day, and then sleep in the next day. You have to walk the dog twice a day no matter how tired you are, and no matter what you're up to today. Day by day it was getting harder and harder to resist the temptation to do what I wanted to instead of what I promised to. So, my parents ended up taking care of the dog. And it was no longer MY dog, but it was our FAMILY dog. But I think they didn't mind.

questions: Why do some people fail to keep their promises?
Do children keep their promises?
Do parents in your country make promises to their children?
What kinds of promises do people often make?
Do most people fulfill their promises?
Do you often keep your promises?
Is it useful to write down promises?
Do you think children should be given rewards for keeping promises?
On what occasions do children make promises to their parents?
Do you think it is important to keep a promise?
samples: Well, I guess, on a large scale because they make promises that they simply can't keep. Unfortunately, I know quite a lot of people who are not selective about promises they make. They first promise something and only then think if they are able to fulfill the promise they gave. Though, I'm sure that some people break their promises just because they don't think that unfulfilled promises can hurt the people they made their promises to or because they are unaware that broken promises can spoil their reputation and personal relationships with other people.

I guess they do but only if their parents exemplify integrity themselves, keeping their promises to children and people around. From the time they are born, kids learn how to live in the world by observing and imitating those around them.
Though, I think that parents' own example is not the only way to motivate kids to do what they promised. It's also a good idea for parents to be intentional about how to teach their kids the importance of keeping promises. For example, they can do it by highlighting news items and personalities that illustrate the value of integrity to their children or simply by making it a priority to support their kids' commitments as I'm more than sure that it will be easier for youngsters to keep their promises if they know that parents will give them a hand in case they can't do what they promised someone by themselves. So yeah, kids definitely keep their promises but only if they understand that they are accountable for what they promised and if they know they can always rely on their parents' help.

Of course, they do. Parents in my country promise their kids to love and support them no matter what, trust them in any situation and be there for them whenever they need it. Well, and of course, they promise their children a lot of more down-to-earth things such as come home earlier from work to spend more time together, teach them how to do something they want to learn to do, buy them something they really want, send them somewhere they really want to go and even help them do their homework. Oh, and one more thing, I'm sure that parents' promises to their kids are universal all around the world and do not differ from country to country.

Well, I guess that people often make mostly two types of promises: to themselves and to other people. People often promise to themselves to start keeping to a diet, do sport regularly, go to bed earlier in order to have enough rest during the night. Also, many people promise to spend more time with the family, start planning their budget and stop wasting time on social networks. When dealing with others, people often promise to call somebody, for example, parents, colleagues or friends, visit somebody or help somebody do something important for them. I think these are the most common daily promises people make.

Well, I can't say if most people fulfill their promises or not but one thing is for sure, most people do their best to fulfill their promises because keeping promises is considered a measure of people's worth. There is no doubt that the majority of people understand that breaking promises can be psychologically very taxing as relations are built on promises kept, not on promises broken. What is more, the majority of people know that unfulfilled promises do not only poison their relationships with other people but also damage their own self-esteem getting them caught up in their own failures and disappointments. This explains why I think most people try to keep the majority of promises they give both to others and to themselves.

(1) Yeah, I think writing down promises can actually help a lot. I mean, people forget things all the time, so having promises written down makes them harder to just ignore. Plus, if it's something important like a work deal or money stuff, it's just safer to have proof. And honestly, even for personal things, it kinda makes you take it more seriously. Like, if I promise a friend I'll help them move and actually write it down, I'll feel more obligated to show up. So yeah, I'd say it's a pretty good idea, at least for bigger commitments.

(2) Nah, I don't really think it makes a difference. If someone's gonna keep a promise, they'll do it whether it's written down or not. And if they're not serious about it, no piece of paper is gonna change that. Plus, even if something is written down, people can still break their promises, so it doesn't guarantee anything. Also, in everyday life, we make so many small promises like meeting a friend for coffee or helping someone out. Writing them all down would be impractical and weird. I think trust and communication are more important than putting everything in writing.

Well, I guess they should as my experience shows that behaviours are more likely to happen again when followed by a positive consequence like a reward. I think this is due to the fact that when a child earns a reward, he knows he has done something good and something his parents like.
Though, to my mind, the only way to reward kids for their behaviour is using nonmaterial rewards as rewarding kids with material stuff can fuel a materialistic outlook on life as it encourages kids to place more importance on goods in general. So, when I say about rewarding young ones for keeping promises, I mean such rewards as praise, which will tell a child exactly what behaviour a parent liked, affection like hugs, kisses, a high five or a smile, and attention combined with activities, like for instance, extra time with parents playing a favourite game, going to the movies or even reading a story.

Oh, mostly when they want to get something from their parents or when they want their parents to let them do something parents are not eager to let them do, for example, stay at home instead of going to school on a test day or play computer games instead of reading a book in the evening. I also know children who are ready to promise parents to get the moon on a stick when they want to please their parents or cheer them up in cases when parents are in low spirits or have fallen on hard times. Oh, and of course in the situations when children have done something wrong and try to avoid punishment or tongue-lashing or simply don't want to quarrel with their folks.

Well, definitely it is as fulfilled promises are great for motivation and success. They build a sense of self efficacy and trust in ourselves, and this way help us find a peaceful balance. Also, they impose certain discipline in our life, which keeps us on track to achieve our life goals. While unfulfilled promises can lead to a vicious cycle of failure as they leave open loops and sap our energy. Broken promises always create an emotional reaction of shame and embarrassment, and make us feel discomfort, guilt and a sense of uneasiness, which damages our own self-esteem and destroys our wellbeing. So, keeping promises is undoubtedly very important.

part2.topic: Line from a song or poem
part2.cue: Describe a line (or a few words) that you remember from a song or poem.
points: which song or poem it is from
part2.sample:
Some time ago, I asked my elder sister what music she liked to listen to when she was my age. Soon, I regretted asking this question. Later, you'll understand why. She played some of her favorite songs, and one of them was 'Wannabe' by the Spice Girls. I kind of liked it and decided to listen to it one more time. On the one hand, almost all the words were clear; however, I wasn't able to sing along. The only line I could sing along to was: "So tell me what you want, what you really, really want." To be honest, even now, I don't remember more than that.
Back then, I took it as a challenge. I found the lyrics and tried to read the first verse quickly. Then I attempted to sing along again. Although I could read the lyrics fast, I ran out of breath while trying to keep up with the vocalist. Every time, I ended up slurring my words like a drunk.
I decided not to give up. I told myself, 'Impossible is nothing.' I played the song over and over until I got tired of it. However, all my attempts to sing along with the first verse failed. Later, I realized I had made a fatal mistake by listening to that song on repeat. The next day, I woke up with 'Wannabe' stuck in my head. I kept repeating those few lines from the verse over and over in my mind. I tried listening to other songs, but as soon as one song finished, 'Wannabe' would return, stuck on a loop in my head. I thought I was going to go crazy.
I must say, it's one of the most persistent earworms ever.
Once it buries itself in your brain, it feels like you'd need surgery to remove it once and for all. Out of curiosity, I decided to google more about this girl group. What I found shocked me a little. This song is actually at the top of the list of the catchiest songs of all time. If only I had known that earlier.

questions: What can people learn from songs or poems?
Why do children like the rhythm of songs or poems?
Do you think it is easier for children to learn a song or poem than for adults?
Do you think it is a waste of time for kids to learn songs or poems?
Are you good at memorizing things?
Do you agree that learning history may help people understand the present?
Is it important for kids to learn history at school?
samples:
Well, I think that people can learn nothing if the song or poem doesn't convey anything meaningful. But there are a lot of inspirational songs and poems that people can learn a lot from. First of all, songs that resonate with a person's soul can be very therapeutic. And I'm sure that sometimes listening to inspirational songs is more effective than visiting a psychologist. We all go through bad times, we all experience disappointment, loss, and change, and we all feel sad, anxious, and stressed at various times in our lives.
From time to time all of us feel heart broken, betrayed or depressed. So, listening to inspirational songs or reading poems, people can learn that no matter what they are going through in the present moment, someone else has been there. As a result, they can learn that their problems aren't special or unique and that there's always a way out. Also, people can learn some of the most important life lessons.
For example, people can learn how to live a better life.
Some songs and poems can change the way people see the world. Some songs and poems tell people that rather than lamenting all that is wrong with the world and further spread negativity, hopelessness and inaction, they should dare to take action instead, and if people want to change the world around, they should start with the one person they can directly impact, and that is him or her. There are songs and poems that teach people that the hardest part of any new adventure is the first step. Some songs and poems encourage people to do what makes them happy because in the end, life's too short... and many other useful things

Well, I don't have kids yet; and that's why I don't know much about children's cognitive development and learning.
So I may be wrong, but I think babies respond positively to rhythmic regularity and musical repetition just because beat perception is innate, so beat detection does not require voluntary attention. This means the only thing newborn infants can detect in songs and poems is the beat. And, of course, it is clear that infants recognize the melody of a song long before they understand the words. Or, maybe, fast-paced songs mimic their heart rates. So they like what they are familiar with, what they are used to and what they can understand and perceive easily. Another possible reason is that beat induction is learned in the first few months of life, for example, while parents are rocking the infant. So, maybe, babies associate the rhythm of a song or poem with being lulled or entertained by their parents.

Actually, I think it's really helpful for kids to learn songs or poems. It can improve their memory and help with concentration, which is great for learning in general. Plus, songs and poems are a fun way to learn language, especially for younger kids. It can also boost their creativity and confidence when they perform in front of others. And let's not forget, the rhythm and music can help them remember things better, which can be useful in other subjects too. So overall, I'd say it's a pretty beneficial activity

Yes, I think I can say so. I have no difficulty in memorising information 'cause I use a number of simple memorisation strategies. For example, I always try to review information just before I go to sleep 'cause it has been proved that our brain processes and stores information while we sleep.
Also, I'm an auditory learner, so for me the most effective way to memorise information is by hearing it. So to memorise, say, a poem, I read it out loud to myself several times. Sometimes I record it and then play it again and again.

Absolutely. I'm convinced that the past causes the present.
I mean events in the past have made us what we are today.
So any time we want to know why something happened, whether it be a shift in political party dominance in some country, a major change in the teenage suicide rate, or a war in some part of the world, we need to look further back to identify the causes of the change or event. And we don't need to go far in the search for proof. The evidence is everywhere. We live in societies with complex cultures, rules, traditions, values and religions that have not been created on the spur of the moment. They were created in response to something which happened in the past. Also, communities speak languages that are inherited from the past. And, of course, nowadays people use many things that were invented in the past. If our ancestors hadn't invented, say, the wheel and the internal combustion engine, we would probably still travel on horses or on foot.

For me, a hat is like a cherry on the cake, it always makes my look more complete than that of non-hatted people. I feel like a star... like Elizabeth Tailor or Angelina Jolie... Sometimes I like wearing hats for practical reasons, you know, as a cover-up for bad-hair days. But in the winter, I hate hats as it's absolutely impossible to take them off without messing up a hairdo.

(1) Well, just my old knitted hat which I wear in the winter to keep my head from cold. And, of course, some cap to prevent a heat stroke in the summer. I never buy expensive hats as when I take them off somewhere inside, I quickly forget about them, so I often have to buy new ones, therefore I care neither about their quality nor the style.

(2) I'm a real hat person, so I have a number of hats that come in a variety of shapes and sizes. My favourite type is a fedora hat as it has some magic power to transform any outfit. I always put it onwhen I need to look respectable. I also have a nice flat cap which makes me look incredibly stylish. It's really hard to say as I rarely pay attention to what other people wear. Probably it's much more popular than I think it is. What I've noticed, though, is that many fashion conscious men wear sort of wooly hats and baseball caps.

I'm sure to keep heads warm in the winter and keep from getting a sunburn on the head on hot summer days are the main reasons why most people wear hats and caps. Definitely yes. As a child, whenever I went outside on a cold day, the first thing I heard from my mom was a reminder to put on a hat. I hated that, but I couldn't leave home until my mom had made sure that I'd put one on. In the summer, actually, it was the same story, but with caps.

(1) Like everything I have, I prefer buying hats and caps online First of all, I can find goods at reasonable prices as everyone knows Internet prices are hard to beat. part2.sample:
I'm going to describe a high-rise building which appeared right in the centre of our city last year. It's called X, and everybody says it's the tallest skyscraper in the country. I remember that when I first saw the construction site, I thought it would be nothing more than a concrete cookie-cutter monster, which would just block out the sun. Thank God, my fears didn't materialise, and it appeared to be a very beautiful modern building with original design. It has about 40 storeys. And it's made of tinted glass, shiny steel and concrete like almost all modern buildings nowadays.
This building serves several purposes. On the bottom floor there's a shopping centre, parking space and something else. I don't remember what. It also accommodates some cafes, numerous shops and offices. There are residential units on top floors. Some of them are luxurious and really expensive. There's also a restaurant with a panoramic view of the city. It's a wonderful place for romantic dates.
I like this high-rise building because I perceive it as a symbol of progress in the city. Apart from that, it has become is a notable landmark, which attracts tourists.

questions: Is the appearance of a public building as important as its functionality?
Is it worth spending a lot of money on the appearance of a building?
Is it more important for a building to look good on the outside or on the inside?
Why do people like to visit historical places?
What types of buildings are popular in your country?
samples: Well, to my mind, it is. I am more than sure that there should be a balance between these two important elements. I consider that public buildings are a reflection of who we are as a community and as people, and so should be designed to make a statement about a city in order to attract visitors not only for what goes on inside them, but for the experience of buildings themselves.

(1) Honestly, I think the outside is more important because it's the first thing you notice. I mean, when you're walking through a city, the buildings are what catch your eye, right? If a building looks cool or different, it kind of becomes a landmark and people want to see it or live there. Like, if you think of places like the Burj Khalifa or the Empire State Building, they're not just famous because of what's inside, but because of their amazing exteriors. Plus, the outside of a building often reflects what's inside, so a nice-looking exterior shows that the place is probably well-maintained.
And, let's be real, a building that looks nice on the outside will probably get more attention from people, whether it's customers or tourists. So, yeah, I think the outside definitely matters more.

(2) I actually think the inside is more important because that's where people spend most of their time. If the inside is comfortable and well-designed, it makes a huge difference. I mean, think about it. No one really cares how the outside looks if the inside is cramped or uncomfortable. A cozy, functional space can totally change the vibe, whether it's a home, office, or a shop. And the cool thing is, it's easier to fix up the inside if it needs it, without tearing down the whole building. For example, a bright, open space with nice furniture or good lighting can make people feel more relaxed and productive. So, yeah, I think how the inside feels is way more important than how the outside looks

Oh, I think because historical places give them a more realistic vision of history and enable them to develop a deeper understanding of the people and places that have shaped society today. They help people see the bigger picture as well as grasp the achievements of mankind and bring a great experience of learning new things. All of this makes people happy, creates addiction and pushes them to visit more and more historical sights.

(1) In Saudi Arabia, the most popular buildings are skyscrapers.
Cities like Riyadh and Jeddah have impressive high-rise buildings, such as the Kingdom Centre Tower. There's also a growing demand for luxury hotels, especially in Mecca and Medina, to accommodate pilgrims. Shopping malls are very popular as well. Places like the Red Sea Mall in Jeddah are full of life, with a variety of stores and entertainment options. And, of course, modern villas and palaces are common in wealthier areas. Many have large outdoor spaces and private pools.

(2) In the Philippines, high-rise buildings are very popular, especially in cities like Manila and Cebu. With the country's growing population, people are moving into condos and apartment complexes that offer convenience and amenities.
In my country, beach resorts are really popular, especially in tourist spots like Boracay. People love the beautiful beaches and the luxury hotels there. And while many people live in urban areas, there are still traditional bamboo houses in rural regions that are eco-friendly and perfectly suited for the tropical climate.
