questions: How do we choose gifts?
What do you consider when choosing a gift?
What kind of gifts are popular in your country?
What's the best gift you have ever received?
What gift have you received recently?
Do you like to give expensive gifts?
How often do you buy gifts for other people?
Why do people give gifts?
Have you ever received a gift which you didn't like?
samples: When picking gifts for friends or family, we typically begin by thinking about what they like. For example, if the recipient is into gardening, we might look for a nice plant or gardening tools. It's all about finding something that resonates with their hobbies and preferences.

Well, people in my country really like to give books and handmade gifts as well as home décor presents such as frames, figurines and candles. All these things create comfort and remind the receiver of the giver's love and affection. Many people also give flowers and chocolates, especially as "Thank you" presents and cash as a birthday or wedding gift.

Oh no, I don't. Expensive gifts mean more pressure on my monthly expense, which, in turn, means I will have to refuse from something I really need in order to please another person with something costly. What is more, I don't want to buy anybody's love with material things. I'd better do it with actions.
Oh, I actually do it quite often. I would even say almost every day. Just because I like to show thoughtfulness, love and affection to close people and raise a smile on their faces.

I guess there are a lot of reasons why people do it. For example, to show interest and appreciation, or express gratitude to others. People also give gifts to mark milestones and just bring joy and pleasure to the ones they love.

Oh yeah, it happened to me a while ago. I got a key box from my mate which I didn't like at all as it was big and heavy enough and I just couldn't come up with an idea when and where to use it. And still, I struggled to bring a smile to my face to show gratitude to the giver as any present,/u>, to my mind, is worth a 'thank you'.

questions: Do you think your home is clean and tidy?
What housework do you dislike?
What housework do you like?
Do you often do housework?
Do you have breakfast at home every day?
Do you want to learn how to cook well?
Do you like cooking?
Who usually does the cooking in your home?
samples:
(1) I guess it looks clean most of the time. First of all, I try to keep the main surfaces clean. Plus, there are no stains in shower, tub or sink fixtures. There are no crumbs or dirt on the floor. My sink is always empty and clean - there are never dirty dishes in it. And what's important is that everything has a place and is in the place it belongs. I'd say my home is clean enough for guests to visit unexpectedly.

(2) It's super clean. I clean my house on a regular basis to maintain a healthy living environment 'cause dust is a very common cause for colds, coughs, asthma attacks, breathing and respiratory problems, and various types of allergies. Plus, Ilike when it's clean enough to be prepared for surprise visitors.

(3) Oh, my house is constantly messy no matter how hard I try to keep it clean. The thing is that I have a cat. So everything is covered with my cat's hair, so much that it's like a snowstorm in my house. And I'm constantly finding fur everywhere. No matter how often I vacuum it just keeps coming back. It's like a never-ending battle.

(4) I wish it were, but I just don't have time for a cleaning routine. I work full time, and in the evenings I feel so tired that cleaning is what I want to do least. Plus, I have two kids, and they are messmakers. They throw toys around, play with their arts and crafts materials on the floor, and run around like crazy.

(1) What I hate is vacuuming! I think it's because of the noise and monotonous nature of pushing a vacuum around. It just gets on my nerves and bores me to death. Another reason why I hate doing this chore is that I don't like having to move furniture and reach into all the far corners of my house. Plus, every time I vacuum, dust and pet dander get stirred up into the air and make me sneeze and itch. So it's not only a chore that I dread, but it also causes me physical discomfort.

(2) The chore I hate is washing the dishes. It's one of those things that needs to be done every single day, and it's a big pain 'cause I have a lot of pots and pans to clean. Plus, it takes so long because I have to scrub each dish separately. What makes it worse for me is that my hands are always so dry after I finish. But I just can't get used to using gloves.

(3) What I really hate is doing the dishes. So I just say to myself that I will do them tomorrow and just let them pile up. But as you know 'tomorrow never comes'. And the longer I procrastinate, the harder it is to make myself do the chore.
As a result, every day, they slowly accumulate... Lots of plates covered in sauces and crumbs, bowls with a layer of sticky who-knows-what, forks, knives, and spoons all gummed with bits of this and that.

(1) It may sound weird, but I love washing the dishes. It's one of my favorite chores! First of all, doing repetitive motions is calming. I would even say it's therapeutic to me. And I normally use this time to practice mindfulness. I mean, I try to focus on the task at hand, and it helps me clear my mind and relax. Plus, I enjoy listening to the soft sounds of the water running and the gentle clinking of dishes against each other as I wash them. It's like a mini-meditation session for me.

(2) My favourite chore is washing the dishes. First of all, it's a great way to show my family how much I care about them and our home. Plus, when it's all done, I get that feeling of accomplishment and satisfaction when I look at sparkling clean dishes in a freshly wiped sink. And it can be fun. Sometimes I sing along to my favorite songs while washing the dishes and it makes the chore seem less tedious. Sometimes I listen to podcasts and audiobooks. So it can be educational as well.

(3) What I really enjoy is washing the dishes although most people consider it to be a mundane task. But for me, it's like a mini-mediation session. One of the best parts about it is the sound of running water and clinking dishes. The sound of running water creates background noise that blocks out other distractions. The sound of clinking dishes, on the other hand, helps create a calming atmosphere. And I can use this time to focus on my thoughts and feelings without any distractions from other people or technology

No, I don't always have breakfast at home. Sometimes I'm in a rush and I'll grab something quick on the go, like a granola bar or a piece of fruit. Other times, I'll stop at a cafe and get something more substantial, like a breakfast sandwich or a bowl of oatmeal. It just depends on my schedule and what I'm in the mood for

(1) Yeah, I'd love to. If I learn to cook like a pro, I will be able to experiment with different flavors, ingredients, and cooking techniques to create dishes that are truly unique and tailored specifically towards my tastes and preferences.
But, in my opinion, learning how to cook well isn't just about making delicious dishes it's also about eating healthier meals made with fresh ingredients 'cause I will know exactly what ingredients I'm using and how much of each one. Plus, it can save me quite a bit of money 'cause home-cooked meals can be a lot cheaper than buying food at restaurants or getting take out.

(2) Well, cooking is not my thing 'cause it takes too much time and effort. I mean, why bother when there are so many delicious options out there? Stores are filled with readymade meals that are just as tasty. And I can go to a cafe or restaurant whenever I want to. Plus, I don't think I have the patience or skill to cook complicated dishes. And it's not like it's necessary for survival or anything. There are just too many other things that I'd rather do with my time.

Oh yes, I adore it. Cooking at home is always a fun time with my family 'cause we like to cook together. It also lets me control my family's health. What's more, it lets me save money as I have a choice about where and how many products to buy. One more thing I can add is that homemade food tastes much better, especially when I see happy faces of my beloved ones enjoying the meal.

Well, I am the one who always cooks in my home. I do it because I adore cooking and because I am really good at it.
I can easily make a great meal out of random fridge ingredients, and it makes life easy for all my family members. One more reason why I cook for everyone is the fact that I have enough time for that. Though, from time to time my husband and kids help me in the kitchen but not more often than once a week, to my regret.

part2.cue: Describe a plan you had to change.
points: why you had to change it
how you felt about the change
part2.sample:
Last Saturday, I was so excited because I planned to go to my friend's birthday party. I even bought a new shirt for the occasion. I imagined how fun the party would be music, food, and catching up with everyone. But on Friday night, everything changed. I started feeling a bit strange. My throat felt scratchy, and I sneezed a few times, but I thought, 'Oh, it's nothing. I'll be fine tomorrow.'
However, when I woke up on Saturday morning, I felt terrible. My head was heavy, my nose wouldn't stop running, and I had a terrible cough. I checked my temperature, and it was higher than normal. I knew right away I couldn't go to the party like this. I felt so disappointed. I was really looking forward to seeing my friends, eating cake, and celebrating together. But I also didn't want to ruin the party by coughing everywhere or making someone else sick. I texted my friend and told her I couldn't come. So instead of going out, I spent the day at home. I stayed in my pajamas, drank hot tea with honey, and watched a few old movies. My mom even made me some chicken soup, which was really comforting. Even though I missed the party, I knew it was the right decision to stay home and rest.

questions: Why do parents still make plans for their children nowadays?
How does technology help people make plans?
Do old people often change plans?
Do young people like to change plans?
What are the common reasons when people need to change plans?
How would you tell your friends if you had to change your plans?
samples: I think that parents still make plans for their kids because they want to make sure they have the best opportunities, like with school or their future job. Kids don't always know what's best, so parents step in to guide them. Plus, they want to keep them safe and out of trouble, especially when they're young. It's also a way for parents to make sure kids develop good habits, like sticking to a routine or getting involved in activities. Parents want to give them stability and structure so they feel secure. And of course, they want them to succeed, so they plan ahead for their future. At the end of the day, it's about helping kids navigate life and teaching them how to plan.

Well, technology just makes planning way easier. With Google Calendar, we can set reminders for meetings and deadlines, so we don't miss anything. Google Maps helps us figure out the best routes, avoid traffic, and save time.
Apps like WhatsApp make it super easy to organize plans with people without all the back-and-forth messages. And if we're traveling, Triplt keeps all our flight and hotel info in one place. Basically, tech just takes care of all the little details, so planning feels way less stressful.

Oh no. I don't think they do. As my experience shows they only do it when something goes wrong along the way, for example, if they suddenly feel bad or find out that their children or grandchildren need their help or care. In other situations old people never change their plans as they are very responsible, on the one hand, and are afraid of any changes, on the other hand.

Well, I think the majority of them do as new plans usually bring new beginnings, adventure and excitement to life, which the young like. What's more, changes break up the routine opening new opportunities and helping younger generation get out of a rut. Though, I am sure there are young people who hate changing plans as they have an instinctive fear of the unknown or just because any change causes stress and washes them out.

Well, I think in most common cases people need to change their plans when something goes wrong along the way and the plans they had just fail. It can happen when their plans are connected with something beyond their control or depend on other people and their decisions. One more widespread reason for changing plans is seeing better alternatives or getting more pleasure.

Well, it depends on the plans, first of all, and on whether my plans are connected with my friends or impact them somehow. If these plans concerned only me and didn't influence my pals in a negative way, I think I would just invite them for coffee and tell about the changes I've made.
But if these plans were somehow connected with my friends and affected their interests, I would definitely choose the most appropriate time and place and do my best to explain why I've made a decision like this. Anyway, it would be better if they learnt about it from me but not from somebody else.

questions: What apps have you used recently?
What apps are you usually interested in?
What apps would you like to use in the future?
How much time do you spend on these apps?
samples: Well, I think all possible kinds. I have a couple of news apps because it's important for me to keep up with current events and know what is happening in my city, country and in the world. I also have a few games just to relax and get my mind off troubles or pass the time while waiting for somebody or queuing. As I am a business person I have to have some apps for business too, for example, email apps, apps for editing documents, reminders, notepad apps, a currency converter and a calculator to be able to do my work wherever I am, even on the go. Oh, I almost forgot to name a weather app, a photo editor, an alarm clock, some trip planners, a few social networks, some music and video apps. Yeah, that's it. Pretty much stuff, actually What is more, I can organize travel information, manage my business and even track my spending habits. I guess this is what explains why I spend that much time on applications.

Well, sometimes it seems to me that I spend around 80% of my free time on them and it frightens me a lot because I almost don't have any time left for active rest with friends and family members. What's worse is I don't do anything to change the situation because the more I use apps, the less I want to stop using them. Apps open so many opportunities and let me do so much stuff just with the help of my phone. I can do shopping, swap messages with friends, listen to music and even watch some film or video on my phone.

questions: Do you mind noises?
Do any noises bother you?
Do you think there's too much noise in modern society?
Are cities becoming noisier?
Where is there louder noise, in cities or in the countryside?
What type of noise do you come across in your daily life?
Are there any sounds that you like?
samples: I would say I'm pretty tolerant to noises when I'm not asleep as I've learned to cut out the unwanted ones. But when I am about to fall asleep, I become very sensitive to any kind of noise, and nearly anything can make me irritated Sometimes I toss and turn throughout the night just because I hear the muffled sound of slammed doors in the flat next door.

There's no worse noise than scraping chalk on a blackboard. You know, many cafes still use such boards as an advertising medium. When I see them, I can't help imagining the way this information was written down. And even the thought of it makes me feel sick.

Yeah, the level of noise is getting higher and higher. In fact, it is so high that it is now regarded a type of environmental pollution. This is because nowadays cities are more crowded than in the past, which means that there's much more traffic on roads. There are more people talking everywhere. Oh, and I nearly forgot to mention air conditioning equipment which is one of the biggest parts of all ambient noise in today's cities.

We are surrounded by different sounds both indoors and outdoors. My typical day starts with the sound of boiling water as I can't imagine my morning without a cup of coffee. Every single day I'm accompanied by roaring engines, slammed doors, mouse clicking and constantly ringing phones

Oh yeah! Splashing waves and screams of sea-gulls sound like music to me. I also enjoy the sound of rain when I'm inside and don't have to go anywhere. And I can't help mentioning the train tracks clanking in a constant pattern This sound makes me fall asleep as soon as the train leaves

part2.cue: Describe a time when it was important to tell your friend the truth.
points: why it was important to tell the truth
part2.sample:
Well, last year I went to a winter resort, and I needed a big suitcase 'cause I couldn't cram all my winter stuff into my small one. You know, just one sweater took up half the space. So I decided to borrow a bigger one 'cause I didn't want to buy an item that I would use once in a blue moon. I have a friend from work who is a serial traveller, and he has suitcases of all sizes and shapes. So I decided to borrow a suitcase from him. The one that he gave to me was hardside luggage. This made me a little worried. These suitcases are very stylish, but prone to cracking and damage. And they are particularly vulnerable to damage during carriage on an airplane while being loaded and unloaded. They do not like being thrown around as many baggage handlers do. I was really afraid it would be scratched or damaged in any other way.
What I feared came upon me. My luggage was damaged during the flight. I didn't know how to tell my friend about it.
I decided to buy exactly the same suitcase and return it to my friend, hoping he wouldn't notice the change.
I spent a few days searching for it, but this suitcase model was out of stock. So all I could do was tell my friend the truth about his suitcase and offer a replacement item. When I told him the news, he was so upset that he didn't even manage to get the right look on his face. It appeared to be his favourite suitcase. But he wasn't angry with me 'cause it wasn't my fault.

questions: What's the colour you dislike?

What is your favourite colour?
What is the most popular colour in your country?
What colours do your friends like most?
What colour would you never use in your home?
samples: I'm not a big fan of white for a few reasons. First, it gets dirty too easily, and it's hard to keep clean, which can be annoying. Also, in my culture, white is linked to funerals and mourning, so it doesn't feel very cheerful. When it comes to home decoration, having too much white reminds me of a hospital, and it doesn't feel cozy at all. That's why I prefer warmer, more inviting colors.

(1) Yes, I bought a canary yellow bag because everyone said it was the trendiest color. I knew right off the bat I wouldn't use it because I don't really like bright colors, but I still bought it. Now it just sits in my closet.

(2) Yes, I bought a silver dress for a party once. Everyone had to wear silver, so I had no choice. I don't really like silver, but I still bought it. After the party, I never wore it again.

(3) Yes, I saw deep teal leather pumps and bought them. I loved the color, but now I don't wear them because I don't have any clothes that match this color.

(4) Yes, I bought a mint green cushion for my sofa. My living room has some pale green curtains, and I wanted the colors to match. I think it really made the room look better

It is yellow that I like as it seems to exude nothing but warmth and happiness. This is the only colour that makes me feel energetic and elated. I think this is the best colour to signify positive emotions.

(1) I would avoid stimulating colours, for instance, large splashes of red and yellow or sharp contrasting colours such as black and white. This is because my bedroom should be a place of peace and tranquility rather than a stimulating environment.

(2) I would advise against too much black as it will make me feel on the low side or even depressed. Similarly, I would try to avoid red because I will never have deep sleep or possibly have trouble falling asleep as it is not an easy bedroom colour to relax.

part2.cue: Describe a person who shows his or her feelings openly.
points: why you think this person is open
how you feel about this person
part2.sample:
I think that my best friend Ann is a rare example of a person who expresses her feelings freely. We've been friends for many years, and I see her almost every day. So I know what I'm talking about. I mean I have enough evidence to prove that she's an open person. Oh no, to say 'open' is to say nothing. I think she's too open about her feelings. If something is on her mind, she always lets people know about it whether they want it or not. For example, she tells people when something is bothering her, when something makes her feel excited, depressed or uncomfortable. She isn't afraid to tell people about painful or embarrassing situations that she experienced. And I know that she alway says what she means, but not what other people want to hear. What's more, she posts a lot of personal details on Facebook and Instagram. I always joke that if we stopped being friends, I would still know as much information about her feelings and opinions as I do being her best friend and communicating with her every day.
On the one hand, I admire her ability to open up even to strangers 'cause this helps her connect a lot more with other people. Her openness encourages other people to open up, and this helps to create a more open and trusting environment. Also, Ann is very easy to deal with, and it doesn't take much time to get to know her. When she is offended, she shows it and says that she's offended and explains why. When she's angry or embarrassed, she doesn't hide her emotions as well. Dealing with her doesn't require guesswork to understand what her opinion about something is, whether she's happy or not and why. You know, I find it really stressful and annoying to deal with people who have a blank and emotionless expression on their faces at all times. I can't read anyone's mind. And I don't want to.
On the other hand, I don't think it's good to be an open book all the time. I always tell her that she should be selective about who she tells about herself. First of all, it can be dangerous for her. And this makes her vulnerable.
Also, I think she discloses too much too soon. This turns some people off. I'm sure it would be much better if she kept self-disclosure to conversations with close people. And it seems to me her being too open is the main reason why she's still single. This drives some guys away and makes them lose interest. And I have to say that her openness isn't always appropriate. I mean that by expressing what she is feeling, she not only passes some of her emotion to others, but she also has to be ready to deal with the aftermath of that disclosure. But she isn't.

questions: What kinds of emotional support do people need at work?
Would you share your feelings with your coworkers?
Is it possible to know a job applicant's emotional resilience through the recruiting process?
samples:
I think when it comes to emotional support at work, there are a few key things that really help people. First off, encouragement and praise are huge. Everyone likes to feel appreciated, and a simple 'good job' can really make someone's day. Another important one is help with stress.
Work can get overwhelming sometimes, and it's good to have ways to cope, whether it's through stress-relief programs or just taking a quick break when needed. And lastly, work-life balance is essential. The option to work from home or have flexible hours helps people manage their personal lives better and avoid burnout.

(1) I think I would. To my mind, it's really important to be open with the people you work with. When you share your feelings, it helps build stronger connections, and that makes it easier to work together. Also, when I feel stressed or overwhelmed, talking about it can actually relieve a lot of pressure. I've noticed that when I talk to my coworkers about personal stuff, it helps create a supportive environment. It's not like you're sharing every little detail, but just letting people know where you're coming from can make a huge difference. It's also easier to trust each other, and that trust is key to getting things done as a team.

(2) I've always thought work is a place to be professional, not to bring in personal stuff. Sharing your feelings can sometimes make things awkward, and that's not what I want in a work setting. Also, there's always the risk that your personal issues could get turned into office gossip, and nobody wants that. Plus, not everyone wants to hear about your problems, so it's better to keep things to yourself. I feel like it's important to keep boundaries, and sharing feelings could make me too vulnerable at work. It's just easier for me to focus on the tasks at hand without mixing in personal emotions.

(1) Yeah, I think it's possible. Like, when someone's in an interview, how they handle tough questions can really show a lot. If they stay chill under pressure, that's a good sign they can deal with stress. Also, when you give them feedback, if they don't get defensive and just take it, it shows they're able to handle setbacks. And, if they talk about challenges they've faced and how they got through them,/u>, you can kinda tell if they've got that emotional strength to bounce back when things get tough.

(2) I don't really think it's possible, to be honest. Interviews are stressful, so it's not always a good reflection of how someone will react in real-life situations. Plus, people can fake being calm and collected, even if they're feeling overwhelmed inside. Emotional resilience is something you can only really see over time, not in one interview. Someone might seem totally fine during the interview, but once they start working, they might struggle. It's just hard to tell how someone's really going to handle stress in the long run.

questions: Do you prefer listening to stories or reading them?
Did you love stories in your childhood?
samples:
(1) I prefer listening to stories. It's easy to listen while doing other things, like cooking or walking. Also, listening helps me relax because I don't have to focus on reading. And lastly, a story feels more real and engaging when someone reads it aloud. I mean, hearing the emotions, tone, and voice of the narrator can make the characters and events in the story seem more vivid, as if they're happening right in front of you.

(2) I prefer reading stories. Like to read at my own pace and think deeply about the story. Reading helps me focus and imagine the story in my own way. Plus, I can go back and reread the parts I like, which is easier than finding the same spot when I'm listening.

(3) I prefer reading books because I usually read in bed before I go to sleep. And when I tried listening to audiobooks, I would often fall asleep, and the book would keep playing all night. After that, it was hard to find where I'd left of

(1) Yes, I really loved stories when I was a kid because they were fun and kept me entertained. They let me spend quality time with my family because my parents read to me before bed. And they always made me excited to hear what would happen next.

(2) I didn't really love stories when I was a kid because, to be honest, I wasn't very interested in reading. I had a really hard time sitting still for long periods and staying focusedon something preferred playing outside instead of reading books.

questions: Do you like to wear hats?
What kinds of hats do you have?
Is wearing hats popular in your country?
Why do people wear hats or caps?
Did you use to wear a hat when you were a child?
Where do you like to buy hats?
samples:
(1) Yes and no. While I hate them in the winter, I can't help loving them the rest of the year. I've got a couple of hats for different purposes. For instance, my favourite one isa wonderful wide-brim hat. What I love is the way it frames my face when I wear it further back on my head. For me, a hat is like a cherry on the cake, it always makes my look more complete than that of non-hatted people. I feel like a star... like Elizabeth Tailor or Angelina Jolie... Sometimes I like wearing hats for practical reasons, you know, as a cover-up for bad-hair days. But in the winter, I hate hats as it's absolutely impossible to take them off without messing up a hairdo.

(2) Not really. Not that I'm timid, but I don't like to be in the centre of everybody's attention, which is inevitable when you're surrounded by non-hatted people wherever you are. So I prefer to go bareheaded.

(1) Well, just my old knitted hat which I wear in the winter to keep my head from cold. And, of course, some cap to prevent a heat stroke in the summer. I never buy expensive hats as when I take them off somewhere inside, I quickly forget about them, so I often have to buy new ones, therefore I care neither about their quality nor the style.

(2) I'm a real hat person, so I have a number of hats that come in a variety of shapes and sizes. My favourite type is a fedora hat as it has some magic power to transform any outfit. I always put it onwhen I need to look respectable. I also have a nice flat cap which makes me look incredibly stylish. Also, I have numerous caps, which I wear when I don't want to think about my hairstyle. To tell the truth, hats are my everything.

It's really hard to say as I rarely pay attention to what other people wear. Probably it's much more popular than I think it is. What I've noticed, though, is that many fashion conscious men wear sort of wooly hats and baseball caps.

I'm sure to keep heads warm in the winter and keep from getting a sunburn on the head on hot summer days are the main reasons why most people wear hats and caps. A select few, though, regard them as wonderful fashion accessories which may help them to stand out from the crowd. Oh, and many people have to wear hats as part of a uniform. For instance, cooks wear hats to prevent hair falling into the food. Or, similarly, policemen wear hats so that people could identify them easily.

Definitely yes. As a child, whenever I went outside on a cold day, the first thing I heard from my mom was a reminder to put on a hat. I hated that, but I couldn't leave home until my mom had made sure that I'd put one on. In the summer, actually, it was the same story, but with caps.

(1) Like everything I have, I prefer buying hats and caps online First of all, I can find goods at reasonable prices as everyone knows Internet prices are hard to beat. Another reason is that I can shop anytime. Taking into account the fact that I work long hours, if it weren't for an opportunity to buy clothes and hats online, I would go everywhere naked.

(2) Anywhere, except the Internet. I may buy hats in department stores and even at secondhand stores provided I can try them on. For me, the hat has always been as special an accessory as sunglasses, so I always choose them really carefully.

part2.cue: Describe a piece of equipment that is important in your home.
part2.sample:
One of the most important pieces of equipment in my home is a vacuum cleaner. I've been using it a lot since I decided to adopt a cat.
Several years ago, I saw a kitten sitting alone in the street, shivering in the rain. My heart melted, so I brought it home.
I just couldn't leave it there. But my family wasn't as excited as I was because they knew this meant more housework. I had always tried to avoid helping around the house, and they worried that cat hair would be everywhere. So, I had to promise to vacuum the floors, furniture, and carpets at least three times a week if I wanted to keep the kitten. They even took pity on me and bought a vacuum cleaner specially designed for pet owners. It's a canister model, with the motor and dust collector connected to the vacuum head by a flexible hose. It's a wheeled type and has really strong suction power, so cleaning doesn't take much effort.
It's also compact and lightweight, making it easy to use.
I'm still keeping my promise, so I regularly vacuum all surfaces, using different attachments for different tasks. If it weren't for this vacuum cleaner, the whole flat would be covered in cat hair because my tiny kitten grew into a very fluffy cat. I'm really grateful that humanity invented this household device because it saves me a lot of time and lets me clean the whole flat quickly.

questions: How do we choose gifts?
What do you consider when choosing a gift?
What kind of gifts are popular in your country?
What's the best gift you have ever received?
What gift have you received recently?
Do you like to give expensive gifts?
How often do you buy gifts for other people?
Why do people give gifts?
Have you ever received a gift which you didn't like?
samples: When picking gifts for friends or family, we typically begin by thinking about what they like. For example, if the recipient is into gardening, we might look for a nice plant or gardening tools. It's all about finding something that resonates with their hobbies and preferences.

Well, people in my country really like to give books and handmade gifts as well as home décor presents such as frames, figurines and candles. All these things create comfort and remind the receiver of the giver's love and affection. Many people also give flowers and chocolates, especially as "Thank you" presents and cash as a birthday or wedding gift.

Oh no, I don't. Expensive gifts mean more pressure on my monthly expense, which, in turn, means I will have to refuse from something I really need in order to please another person with something costly. What is more, I don't want to buy anybody's love with material things. I'd better do it with actions.
Oh, I actually do it quite often. I would even say almost every day. Just because I like to show thoughtfulness, love and affection to close people and raise a smile on their faces.

I guess there are a lot of reasons why people do it. For example, to show interest and appreciation, or express gratitude to others. People also give gifts to mark milestones and just bring joy and pleasure to the ones they love.

Oh yeah, it happened to me a while ago. I got a key box from my mate which I didn't like at all as it was big and heavy enough and I just couldn't come up with an idea when and where to use it. And still, I struggled to bring a smile to my face to show gratitude to the giver as any present,/u>, to my mind, is worth a 'thank you'.

questions: Do you think your home is clean and tidy?
What housework do you dislike?
What housework do you like?
Do you often do housework?
Do you have breakfast at home every day?
Do you want to learn how to cook well?
Do you like cooking?
Who usually does the cooking in your home?
samples:
(1) I guess it looks clean most of the time. First of all, I try to keep the main surfaces clean. Plus, there are no stains in shower, tub or sink fixtures. There are no crumbs or dirt on the floor. My sink is always empty and clean - there are never dirty dishes in it. And what's important is that everything has a place and is in the place it belongs. I'd say my home is clean enough for guests to visit unexpectedly.

(2) It's super clean. I clean my house on a regular basis to maintain a healthy living environment 'cause dust is a very common cause for colds, coughs, asthma attacks, breathing and respiratory problems, and various types of allergies. Plus, Ilike when it's clean enough to be prepared for surprise visitors.

(3) Oh, my house is constantly messy no matter how hard I try to keep it clean. The thing is that I have a cat. So everything is covered with my cat's hair, so much that it's like a snowstorm in my house. And I'm constantly finding fur everywhere. No matter how often I vacuum it just keeps coming back. It's like a never-ending battle.

(4) I wish it were, but I just don't have time for a cleaning routine. I work full time, and in the evenings I feel so tired that cleaning is what I want to do least. Plus, I have two kids, and they are messmakers. They throw toys around, play with their arts and crafts materials on the floor, and run around like crazy.

(1) What I hate is vacuuming! I think it's because of the noise and monotonous nature of pushing a vacuum around. It just gets on my nerves and bores me to death. Another reason why I hate doing this chore is that I don't like having to move furniture and reach into all the far corners of my house. Plus, every time I vacuum, dust and pet dander get stirred up into the air and make me sneeze and itch. So it's not only a chore that I dread, but it also causes me physical discomfort.

(2) The chore I hate is washing the dishes. It's one of those things that needs to be done every single day, and it's a big pain 'cause I have a lot of pots and pans to clean. Plus, it takes so long because I have to scrub each dish separately. What makes it worse for me is that my hands are always so dry after I finish. But I just can't get used to using gloves.

(3) What I really hate is doing the dishes. So I just say to myself that I will do them tomorrow and just let them pile up. But as you know 'tomorrow never comes'. And the longer I procrastinate, the harder it is to make myself do the chore.
As a result, every day, they slowly accumulate... Lots of plates covered in sauces and crumbs, bowls with a layer of sticky who-knows-what, forks, knives, and spoons all gummed with bits of this and that.

(1) It may sound weird, but I love washing the dishes. It's one of my favorite chores! First of all, doing repetitive motions is calming. I would even say it's therapeutic to me. And I normally use this time to practice mindfulness. I mean, I try to focus on the task at hand, and it helps me clear my mind and relax. Plus, I enjoy listening to the soft sounds of the water running and the gentle clinking of dishes against each other as I wash them. It's like a mini-meditation session for me.

(2) My favourite chore is washing the dishes. First of all, it's a great way to show my family how much I care about them and our home. Plus, when it's all done, I get that feeling of accomplishment and satisfaction when I look at sparkling clean dishes in a freshly wiped sink. And it can be fun. Sometimes I sing along to my favorite songs while washing the dishes and it makes the chore seem less tedious. Sometimes I listen to podcasts and audiobooks. So it can be educational as well.

(3) What I really enjoy is washing the dishes although most people consider it to be a mundane task. But for me, it's like a mini-mediation session. One of the best parts about it is the sound of running water and clinking dishes. The sound of running water creates background noise that blocks out other distractions. The sound of clinking dishes, on the other hand, helps create a calming atmosphere. And I can use this time to focus on my thoughts and feelings without any distractions from other people or technology

No, I don't always have breakfast at home. Sometimes I'm in a rush and I'll grab something quick on the go, like a granola bar or a piece of fruit. Other times, I'll stop at a cafe and get something more substantial, like a breakfast sandwich or a bowl of oatmeal. It just depends on my schedule and what I'm in the mood for

(1) Yeah, I'd love to. If I learn to cook like a pro, I will be able to experiment with different flavors, ingredients, and cooking techniques to create dishes that are truly unique and tailored specifically towards my tastes and preferences.
But, in my opinion, learning how to cook well isn't just about making delicious dishes it's also about eating healthier meals made with fresh ingredients 'cause I will know exactly what ingredients I'm using and how much of each one. Plus, it can save me quite a bit of money 'cause home-cooked meals can be a lot cheaper than buying food at restaurants or getting take out.

(2) Well, cooking is not my thing 'cause it takes too much time and effort. I mean, why bother when there are so many delicious options out there? Stores are filled with readymade meals that are just as tasty. And I can go to a cafe or restaurant whenever I want to. Plus, I don't think I have the patience or skill to cook complicated dishes. And it's not like it's necessary for survival or anything. There are just too many other things that I'd rather do with my time.

Oh yes, I adore it. Cooking at home is always a fun time with my family 'cause we like to cook together. It also lets me control my family's health. What's more, it lets me save money as I have a choice about where and how many products to buy. One more thing I can add is that homemade food tastes much better, especially when I see happy faces of my beloved ones enjoying the meal.

Well, I am the one who always cooks in my home. I do it because I adore cooking and because I am really good at it.
I can easily make a great meal out of random fridge ingredients, and it makes life easy for all my family members. One more reason why I cook for everyone is the fact that I have enough time for that. Though, from time to time my husband and kids help me in the kitchen but not more often than once a week, to my regret.

part2.cue: Describe a TV series that you like.
part2.sample:
As far as TV series are concerned, my all-time favourite is the Game of Thrones, a TV drama series based on the epic fantasy novel series, A Song of Fire and Ice. It premiered in 2011, on HBO, but I watched it only last month. By the way, this was the first time I had watched an entire series in one sitting.
The events take place on the fictional continents of Westeros and Essos in a setting that very much resembles the Middle Ages. The main idea is that several noble families fight for control over the mythical lands of Westeros. These families are the Starks of Winterfell, the Lannisters of Casterly Rock, and the Baratheons of Dragonstone. To tell the truth, it's very difficult to say who the main character is as whenever one seems to be taking the lead, they are killed off.
What I really like is that this TV series has a really compelling plot, and I was always on the edge of my seat waiting to see what would happen next. Also, it's really thought-provoking and shows life as it is. First of all, it contains a lot of violent scenes, and this is what reminds me that our life is not a bed of roses, but a constant struggle. Secondly, it shows that there are countless ways to reach the same goal. All the heroes strive for the same thing, but use absolutely different strategies to achieve the desired result. Another thing that I like is that it is dynamic and not excessively long. There are just 10 episodes in each of the six seasons.
I'm sure this TV series is worth a few hours of your time if you haven't watched it yet.

questions: Do you think parents should limit their children from watching television?
Would your family watch TV together?
What are the differences in television viewing habits between the elderly and the young?
How has technology changed the way people watch television?
What do you think about ads in TV series?
samples:
(1) Yes, I think parents should limit their children from watching TV, because too much screen time just isn't good for kids.
It can really affect their sleep and eyesight. Plus, they spend less time being active or playing outside. And let's be honest, not all shows are good for kids. Some of them can be violent or just full of nonsense. I think it's better when parents set some rules,/u>, like how much TV children can watch a day. It also encourages kids to do other things, for example, read, draw, or just talk with family. So yeah, a bit of TV is okay, but there should be limits.

(2) No, I don't think parents should limit it too much, because TV isn't all bad. There's actually a lot of educational stuff out there. Kids can learn about nature, science, and even improve their English. And sometimes, they just need to relax after school. If parents watch programmes with them, it can even be a fun family thing. I mean, of course they shouldn't watch it all day, but setting strict rules can make them want it even more. I think it's better to teach them how to choose what to watch and when. That way, they learn to manage it on their own.

(1) Yeah, we totally watch TV together, especially in the evenings. It's just a nice way for us to relax after a busy day. We tend to like the same shows, so it's easy to find something we can all enjoy. It brings us closer, you know, when we can laugh about the same things or get into a good conversation about a movie we just watched. Plus, it's part of our routine. Like on weekends, we'll usually pick something to watch as a family. We also love watching documentaries or the news together, just to stay informed and talk about it afterward. It's something we do to unwind and connect, even if it's just sitting together in silence.

(2) Honestly, we don't really watch TV together. We have different schedules, so finding time to sit down as a group is hard. Everyone prefers different kinds of shows, so it's easier to just watch TV separately. Some of us aren't even big fans of TV. They'd rather read or do something else. We spend time together in other ways, like chatting or playing games, which I think works better for us. When we do watch TV, it's usually on our own devices, like phones or laptops, rather than all sitting in front of the same screen.
And yeah, sometimes it's just a matter of not having enough time to all gather in one place. We're kind of busy with different things, so TV is just not a big part of our family time.

Well, there are quite a few differences, actually. For one, the type of content is different. The elderly often prefer news, talk shows, documentaries, or classic movies, while young people are more into series, reality shows, Youtube content, and entertainment. Another big difference is the platform: older people usually watch TV on a traditional television set, but young people tend to use smartphones, tablets, or laptops, and they go for streaming services like Netflix, YouTube, or TikTok. The viewing time is also different. Older people might watch TV more regularly and at fixed times, like after lunch or in the evening, while younger people watch whenever they want since they prefer on-demand content. Their viewing habits are different too: the elderly might watch TV passively, kind of like background activity, but younger viewers often binge-watch shows or go for short clips with high engagement.
And the purpose of watching is not the same. Older people might use TV for company, background noise, or just to feel connected to the world, while young people usually watch it for fun, distraction, or relaxation. Also, older people might watch with their spouse or family, but young people often watch alone or talk about shows online with friends.

Oh, it's changed a lot, honestly. These days, people can watch shows anytime and anywhere. They don't have to wait for a certain time like before. Streaming services like Netflix and YouTube have pretty much replaced traditional TV for many people. Also, you don't even need a TV set now. Most people just use their phones, tablets, or laptops to watch programmes. And there's way more control. You can pause, rewind, skip the ads, or even binge-watch an entire season in one night. It's also more personalized now, since apps recommend shows based on what you like, and you can even have your own profile. Plus, social media plays a big role. People talk about what they're watching online, share opinions, or get suggestions from friends. So yeah, watching TV has become way more flexible and interactive than it used to be

To be honest, I don't really like ads in TV series. They totally interrupt the story and kind of ruin the mood, especially if something emotional or dramatic is happening. They also waste time. You're just sitting there waiting for the show to come back. And what's worse is when the same ads play over and over again - it gets really annoying. But at the same time, I get that ads help keep some platforms free, so not everyone has to pay for a subscription. Still, a lot of people prefer streaming services with no ads or they just fast-forward through them if they can. Personally, I usually mute them or grab a snack while they're on. That said, every now and then an ad is actually kind of clever or funny, and sometimes you even discover something useful. But overall, I think most people would rather watch without them.

questions: Do you mind noises?

part2.cue: Describe a puzzle that you solved.
points: how long it took to complete it
whether it was difficult or easy
part2.sample:
Well, when I was a child, I was a jigsaw puzzle enthusiast. I assembled puzzles whenever I had a spare moment. But after I had completed a 5000-piece gradient puzzle, I lost interest in this activity. Since then I've been given lots of them, but they are still unopened, collecting dust on some shelf.
The only puzzle that I have completed since childhood was a 3D wooden mechanical pendulum clock puzzle that my friend gave me for my birthday last year. I was really excited 'cause it was something new for me. And I was hoping it would be challenging as well. I thought it would take me a while to assemble it, but it took me a minute to figure out the process. And once you have the hang of it, it's super easy and lots of fun. So I put it together, all by myself in just a few hours. There were easy to follow instructions. And needed neither glue nor scissors to put it together. The only challenge I faced was that some pieces required a good deal of hand strength to snap together. But it was good 'cause they snapped together perfectly, making it almost impossible to break apart once its assembled.
So even though it wasn't extremely challenging, I enjoyed solving it 'cause doing jigsaw puzzles is a really good way to unwind after a hard working day and spend quality time on your own.

questions: Why do parents let their children play puzzles?
What kinds of puzzles improve people's intelligence?
Why are detective stories attractive to people?
Which is better, a detective movie or its original novel?
Are mind games like crossword puzzle games popular in your country?
Why do people like mind games?
Why do people like digital mind games?
Why do people like digital puzzles?
samples: Well, I think parents do so because they understand that puzzles can be a valuable tool for children to learn new things as well as keep the mind active and working. What is more, it is common knowledge that puzzles present many benefits for children's development. For example, kids develop hand-eye coordination, enhance the large movements of kids to the point where they can then work on their fine motor skills, which leads to better handwriting and typing skills. Also, puzzles give children the chance to use adaptable thinking, deduction and reasoning skills as kids figure out how to put the puzzle together. Well, and one more benefit of playing puzzles is the fact that they deepen children's understanding of how to follow directions to achieve their goals. I guess these are the main reasons why parents let their kids do puzzles.

Well, unfortunately, I'm not well-versed in mind-teasers and know not that many kinds of puzzles but among those kinds which I know, I would give prominence to logic puzzles, sudoku puzzles and crosswords as they exercise parts of the brain that may not be stimulated otherwise and this way increase our neuroplasticity or, in other words, improve our intelligence. Also, these kinds of puzzles require thinking in unconventional ways with given constraints in mind, which boosts our brain activity in general and logical thinking in particular. So yeah, I think that these are the puzzles which improve our intelligence more than any other mindgames.

Well, for me an original novel is much better than a detective movie. The first reason why it is so is because novels give in-depth understanding of characters and plot while movies are more a kind of summary of books. What is more, while reading a novel I always pay attention to every line, imagine how things are going and create the scenes in my head in fine detail. When it comes to movies I just see everything as it is without giving my imagination a chance to fill my head with amazing pictures which usually far exceed the visual effects displayed in movies. And the last reason why I love original novels more than films is because watching a movie is quite quick while reading a novel is a lengthy process which makes me even more involved in the plot and extends my pleasure.

Oh yeah, they are as they provide people with an opportunity to unplug and give themselves and family an escape from the information overload that is buzzing through the very fabric of our lives 24 by Z. The reason why I'm saying 'themselves and family is because mind games are both a great way to spend quality time alone and connect with family while working toward a shared goal.
Well, and one more reason why puzzle games are so popular in my country is because they are a kind of mental workout that improves people's problem-solving skills and attention span which are of primary importance for those who want to succeed in our busy, competitive world.

Well, I think that, first of all, people like mind games because these games help them evaporate the stress of everyday life giving them a kind of an escape from the information overload that is buzzing through the very fabric of modern life 24 by Z. So, first of all, people use puzzles as a great meditation tool and stress reliever in the contemporary world. The second reason why people opt for mind games, as it strikes me, is because mind games are a great way to spend quality time both alone and with close people. Well, and one more reason which explains people's interest in puzzles is the fact that mind games are a kind of mental workout that improves people's problem-solving skills and attention span which are of primary importance for those who want to succeed in our busy, competitive world.

Well, I think, first of all, this is because digital games are easily accessible, I mean that they are either low-cost or free and can be downloaded in a matter of seconds. Also, they are a great way to fight boredom while commuting, waiting in lines, or during other uninteresting routines. Also, these games can be played on the go and they don't take up much of people's time. Well, and the last reason I'd like to mention is that going digital can help the environment as digital copies do not have all those paper covers, paper instruction booklets or cardboard cartons that are very slow to decompose. These are the main reasons, to my mind.

part2.cue: Describe a person who helps to protect the environment.
points: how this person protects the environment
whether it is easy or difficult for this person
how you feel about this person
part2.sample:
The person I just have to tell you about is my colleague Diana. She's of the few people who really care about the environment. Of course, she doesn't do things on a large scale. But even the small things she does make a real difference in our city. She thinks each of us can (and should) take initiative to change what we feel is wrong in our society, neighbourhood, or workplace. For example, recently she declared war on paper waste in our office. My colleagues used to waste a lot of paper. They used to print anything and everything, so there were unused copies all over the place. To be honest, I was guilty of this too and often mad copies I didn't need at all.
One day, she gathered all the employees and talked to us about paper waste. I was blown away to learn that it takes an average of five liters of water to produce a single A4 sheet. She also spoke about the depletion of natural resources, paper pollution, and other serious consequences of mindless paper use. Then, she put up posters with these eye-opening facts all around the office to encourage people to switch to electronic documents whenever possible and to think twice before printing anything. And it worked for us.
Beyond the office, she also helps protect the environment by organizing community cleanups in her neighborhood, and I know that many people support her efforts. I really admire her because I think her contribution is invaluable. I wish there were more people like her. I mean people who understand that we shape society, so it's un to us to make it better.

How can recycling help the environment?

What is the importance of environmental education?
Is it important to teach students environmental protection at school?
Do you think it is necessary to make environmental protection as a subject?
samples: A firm 'yes' as it reduces the pollution caused by waste as well conserves energy. It also reduces the need for raw materials so that the rainforests can be preserved. It lets both people and companies benefit reducing landfills and the amount of unhealthy greenhouse gas emissions, and this way improving health of the former, and reducing financial expenditure thanks to saving energy for the latter. So, recycling is definitely very important in our present-day world.

Well, I guess, first of all, because the recycling message has reached more people. People have understood that many of the resources that are used to produce products and packaging in the modern world are finite, and that synthetic waste that isn't recycled is causing serious problems with health, the weather, and the eco-system generally. People now know that everybody wins with recycling, which also explains why more and more of them have started taking responsibility for their waste. Oh, and one more thing that has gained growing interest for recycling is the fact that authorities in many cities have started to arrange collections of recyclable waste, making it more comfortable for people to address the issue of ensuring a greener future for the generations to come.

Oh, to my mind, environmental education is of great importance these days as it raises awareness of issues impacting the environment imparting knowledge about the current situation and future prospects of nature. What is more, it helps learners see the interconnectedness of social, ecological, economic, cultural and political issues building knowledge and skills necessary to address complex environmental issues. It promotes tolerance of different points of view and different cultures, and helps foster a new generation of informed consumers, workers, as well as policy or decision-makers. So, no doubt, it is difficult to overestimate the significance of this type of education.

Definitely yes as appreciation and understanding of the natural environment surrounding us begins at a young age.
What is more, children are naturally curious and open to learning about nature. They can be very quick to grasp problems and are able to apply energy and enthusiasm to putting solutions in place. So, the earlier they get engaged in real world issues, the faster they can make a difference, changing environmental conditions for the better.

Oh yes, I am sure it is as the environment supports the life of each and every living thing on earth and if they destroy the environment, it will destroy them. The earlier individuals are aware of environmental issues, the deeper understanding of these issues they will have and the earlier they will engage in wise ways of preserving the environment. Studying environmental protection as a subject might push students to start taking action, which is great as children are often reported to be better at getting going with environmental solutions than the adults are.

part2.cue: Describe a sport you really like.
points: how you learned to do it
part2.sample:
My all-time favorite sport is basketball. I've loved it ever since I was a kid. No one actually taught me how to play. I just kind of figured it out. I also watched NBA games from time to time, and I'd try to copy moves from the players. These days, I don't play as often as I'd like to because I have so much on my plate with work and other responsibilities. But whenever I do get the chance, I really enjoy it. You're running, jumping, and always moving, so it's a great workout. At the same time, it never feels like just exercise because you're focused on the game. And it's fun. Another reason I love basketball is that it's a great way to compete and spend time with friends. I'm a pretty competitive person, so I enjoy challenging myself and trying to win. questions: How do we choose gifts?
What do you consider when choosing a gift?
What kind of gifts are popular in your country?
What's the best gift you have ever received?

Do you like to give expensive gifts?
How often do you buy gifts for other people?
Why do people give gifts?
Have you ever received a gift which you didn't like?
samples: When picking gifts for friends or family, we typically begin by thinking about what they like. For example, if the recipient is into gardening, we might look for a nice plant or gardening tools. It's all about finding something that resonates with their hobbies and preferences.

Well, people in my country really like to give books and handmade gifts as well as home décor presents such as frames, figurines and candles. All these things create comfort and remind the receiver of the giver's love and affection. Many people also give flowers and chocolates, especially as "Thank you" presents and cash as a birthday or wedding gift.

Oh no, I don't. Expensive gifts mean more pressure on my monthly expense, which, in turn, means I will have to refuse from something I really need in order to please another person with something costly. What is more, I don't want to buy anybody's love with material things. I'd better do it with actions.
Oh, I actually do it quite often. I would even say almost every day. Just because I like to show thoughtfulness, love and affection to close people and raise a smile on their faces.

I guess there are a lot of reasons why people do it. For example, to show interest and appreciation, or express gratitude to others. People also give gifts to mark milestones and just bring joy and pleasure to the ones they love.

Oh yeah, it happened to me a while ago. I got a key box from my mate which I didn't like at all as it was big and heavy enough and I just couldn't come up with an idea when and where to use it. And still, I struggled to bring a smile to my face to show gratitude to the giver as any present,/u>, to my mind, is worth a 'thank you'.

questions: Do you think your home is clean and tidy?
What housework do you dislike?
What housework do you like?
Do you often do housework?
Do you have breakfast at home every day?
Do you want to learn how to cook well?
Do you like cooking?
Who usually does the cooking in your home?
samples:
(1) I guess it looks clean most of the time. First of all, I try to keep the main surfaces clean. Plus, there are no stains in shower, tub or sink fixtures. There are no crumbs or dirt on the floor. My sink is always empty and clean - there are never dirty dishes in it. And what's important is that everything has a place and is in the place it belongs. I'd say my home is clean enough for guests to visit unexpectedly.

(2) It's super clean. I clean my house on a regular basis to maintain a healthy living environment 'cause dust is a very common cause for colds, coughs, asthma attacks, breathing and respiratory problems, and various types of allergies. Plus, Ilike when it's clean enough to be prepared for surprise visitors.

(3) Oh, my house is constantly messy no matter how hard I try to keep it clean. The thing is that I have a cat. So everything is covered with my cat's hair, so much that it's like a snowstorm in my house. And I'm constantly finding fur everywhere. No matter how often I vacuum it just keeps coming back. It's like a never-ending battle.

(4) I wish it were, but I just don't have time for a cleaning routine. I work full time, and in the evenings I feel so tired that cleaning is what I want to do least. Plus, I have two kids, and they are messmakers. They throw toys around, play with their arts and crafts materials on the floor, and run around like crazy.

(1) What I hate is vacuuming! I think it's because of the noise and monotonous nature of pushing a vacuum around. It just gets on my nerves and bores me to death. Another reason why I hate doing this chore is that I don't like having to move furniture and reach into all the far corners of my house. Plus, every time I vacuum, dust and pet dander get stirred up into the air and make me sneeze and itch. So it's not only a chore that I dread, but it also causes me physical discomfort.

(2) The chore I hate is washing the dishes. It's one of those things that needs to be done every single day, and it's a big pain 'cause I have a lot of pots and pans to clean. Plus, it takes so long because I have to scrub each dish separately. What makes it worse for me is that my hands are always so dry after I finish. But I just can't get used to using gloves.

(3) What I really hate is doing the dishes. So I just say to myself that I will do them tomorrow and just let them pile up. But as you know 'tomorrow never comes'. And the longer I procrastinate, the harder it is to make myself do the chore.
As a result, every day, they slowly accumulate... Lots of plates covered in sauces and crumbs, bowls with a layer of sticky who-knows-what, forks, knives, and spoons all gummed with bits of this and that.

(1) It may sound weird, but I love washing the dishes. It's one of my favorite chores! First of all, doing repetitive motions is calming. I would even say it's therapeutic to me. And I normally use this time to practice mindfulness. I mean, I try to focus on the task at hand, and it helps me clear my mind and relax. Plus, I enjoy listening to the soft sounds of the water running and the gentle clinking of dishes against each other as I wash them. It's like a mini-meditation session for me.

(2) My favourite chore is washing the dishes. First of all, it's a great way to show my family how much I care about them and our home. Plus, when it's all done, I get that feeling of accomplishment and satisfaction when I look at sparkling clean dishes in a freshly wiped sink. And it can be fun. Sometimes I sing along to my favorite songs while washing the dishes and it makes the chore seem less tedious. Sometimes I listen to podcasts and audiobooks. So it can be educational as well.

(3) What I really enjoy is washing the dishes although most people consider it to be a mundane task. But for me, it's like a mini-mediation session. One of the best parts about it is the sound of running water and clinking dishes. The sound of running water creates background noise that blocks out other distractions. The sound of clinking dishes, on the other hand, helps create a calming atmosphere. And I can use this time to focus on my thoughts and feelings without any distractions from other people or technology

No, I don't always have breakfast at home. Sometimes I'm in a rush and I'll grab something quick on the go, like a granola bar or a piece of fruit. Other times, I'll stop at a cafe and get something more substantial, like a breakfast sandwich or a bowl of oatmeal. It just depends on my schedule and what I'm in the mood for

(1) Yeah, I'd love to. If I learn to cook like a pro, I will be able to experiment with different flavors, ingredients, and cooking techniques to create dishes that are truly unique and tailored specifically towards my tastes and preferences.
But, in my opinion, learning how to cook well isn't just about making delicious dishes it's also about eating healthier meals made with fresh ingredients 'cause I will know exactly what ingredients I'm using and how much of each one. Plus, it can save me quite a bit of money 'cause home-cooked meals can be a lot cheaper than buying food at restaurants or getting take out.

(2) Well, cooking is not my thing 'cause it takes too much time and effort. I mean, why bother when there are so many delicious options out there? Stores are filled with readymade meals that are just as tasty. And I can go to a cafe or restaurant whenever I want to. Plus, I don't think I have the patience or skill to cook complicated dishes. And it's not like it's necessary for survival or anything. There are just too many other things that I'd rather do with my time.

Oh yes, I adore it. Cooking at home is always a fun time with my family 'cause we like to cook together. It also lets me control my family's health. What's more, it lets me save money as I have a choice about where and how many products to buy. One more thing I can add is that homemade food tastes much better, especially when I see happy faces of my beloved ones enjoying the meal.

Well, I am the one who always cooks in my home. I do it because I adore cooking and because I am really good at it.
I can easily make a great meal out of random fridge ingredients, and it makes life easy for all my family members. One more reason why I cook for everyone is the fact that I have enough time for that. Though, from time to time my husband and kids help me in the kitchen but not more often than once a week, to my regret.

part2.cue: Describe a live performance you enjoyed watching.
part2.sample:
Some time ago, I watched a breathtaking live acro dance performance on TV. A friend of mine on Facebook sent me a message saying, 'Hurry up! Click the link! An incredible performance is about to start!' It was a live broadcast, so I decided to tune in, thinking I'd just take a short break from work.
At first, there were just two acro dancers moving gracefully across the stage. For the first 30 seconds, nothing extraordinary happened. I was hugely disappointed and was about to close the video when, suddenly, one of the girls did a handstand and landed in a bridge with one leg up. Her toes were perfectly pointed, and her leg was as straight as an arrow. And that's when the magic began.
The other girl, the top partner, quickly mounted her and did a handstand on top of her foot. I gasped in amazement. You should have seen the judges. They were staring at the girls, open-mouthed. Then, the base girl started lifting her other leg up to about 45 degrees. I couldn't believe my eyes.
What I saw completely defied the laws of physics.
They kept going with more mind-blowing double tricks, insane partner handstands, and other gravity-defying acrobatic moves. One of the judges kept repeating, 'How is this even possible?' while the others watched in wide-eyed amazement. The performance was so incredible that I couldn't take my eyes off the stage. And I couldn't help but watch it again and again. I was completely blown away.
To be honest, it's hard to put this experience into words - other than OMG, OMG, OMG! I was so impressed that I even posted about it on my Facebook timeline, which is something I almost never do.

part2.topic: Law you like but want to change
part2.cue: Describe a newly enacted law that you like but you want to change part of it.
points: how you first learned about this law
or, who is affected by this law
explain why you think this is a good law
part2.sample:
In my country, one of the laws introduced in recent years is a smoking ban. It came into effect just a few years ago, which is pretty recent for a law.
I think this ban is one of the smartest laws ever passed. You know, if someone chooses to damage their health, that's their right. I'm fine with that. But it's not fair for nonsmokers to inhale tobacco smoke against their will just because smokers feel like lighting up wherever they please.
So I'm happy that this ban keeps non-smokers away from secondhand smoke, which prevents a range of health issues like respiratory diseases, nausea, and headaches. It has also helped discourage smoking in general. Kids tend to copy what they see adults doing, so the less they see people smoking in public, the lower the chances they'll pick up the habit themselves.
All in all, it's a law that has done a lot of good. But I would take this law even further. I believe there should be stricter fines for littering cigarette butts, since many smokers still toss them on the ground without a second thought.
Cigarette butts are non-biodegradable, and they pollute the soil, clog water systems, and leach dangerous chemicals into the environment. If the government really wants to tackle smoking-related problems, they should address this issue as well.

part2.cue: Describe a sports person or team that you like.
points: how you know about this person
explain why you like this person
part2.sample:
The only sport I enjoy watching, and sometimes even playing, is football. For this reason, of course, my favourite sports star is a football player. He is one of the greatest players of all time. Football experts compare him to the legendary Maradona. And I'm talking about Lionel Messi. He started making headlines many years ago, and he's still very popular.
Messi was born in a small town in Argentina. He was just 5 when he started playing football. When he was a teenager, agents from Barcelona saw his talent, and he moved to Spain. He became one of the youngest players in Barcelona. By the way, in 2021, he announced that he was leaving Barcelona after 21 years of playing for the club (the only club he had played for at that time) 'cause the club said it could no longer afford to pay. It was very emotional, and I even started crying when I saw him crying at his farewell press conference. After that, he played for Paris Saint-Germain for two seasons, and now he plays for Inter Miami in the USA.
He has had a lot of extraordinary achievements and won a lot of trophies so far. For example, in 2022, he won the World Cup with Argentina and was named the best player of the tournament. He also won multiple European Champions League titles and the World Club Championship with Barcelona. What's more, he's Argentina's all-time leading goalscorer.
I love to watch him playing, especially when he scores his beautiful goals from quick counterattacks. He is undoubtedly a natural talent. You know, the ball seems to be glued to his foot. He is a master at reading the game, and he's very quick. Everyone calls him the greatest dribbler of his generation. I particularly like when he dribbles at high speed, then he suddenly slows down, waits for the defender to get closer to him, then accelerates in the opposite direction. It doesn't matter how many defenders try to stop him, it's simply impossible. What's interesting is that everyone knows this trick, but he does it again and again, and defenders always go for that. I can't help admiring Messi because he does things that people talk about years later.

Also, I have numerous caps, which I wear when I don't want to think about my hairstyle. To tell the truth, hats are my everything.

It's really hard to say as I rarely pay attention to what other people wear. Probably it's much more popular than I think it is. What I've noticed, though, is that many fashion conscious men wear sort of wooly hats and baseball caps.

I'm sure to keep heads warm in the winter and keep from getting a sunburn on the head on hot summer days are the main reasons why most people wear hats and caps. A select few, though, regard them as wonderful fashion accessories which may help them to stand out from the crowd. Oh, and many people have to wear hats as part of a uniform. For instance, cooks wear hats to prevent hair falling into the food. Or, similarly, policemen wear hats so that people could identify them easily.

Definitely yes. As a child, whenever I went outside on a cold day, the first thing I heard from my mom was a reminder to put on a hat. I hated that, but I couldn't leave home until my mom had made sure that I'd put one on. In the summer, actually, it was the same story, but with caps.

(1) Like everything I have, I prefer buying hats and caps online First of all, I can find goods at reasonable prices as everyone knows Internet prices are hard to beat. Another reason is that I can shop anytime. Taking into account the fact that I work long hours, if it weren't for an opportunity to buy clothes and hats online, I would go everywhere naked.

(2) Anywhere, except the Internet. I may buy hats in department stores and even at secondhand stores provided I can try them on. For me, the hat has always been as special an accessory as sunglasses, so I always choose them really carefully.

part2.cue: Describe a time when you had a day off, free from work or study.
points: what you did and where you were
part2.sample:
I'm a total workaholic, so I almost never allow myself to step away from my endless to-do lists and take time for myself, even on weekends. But last Friday, I came home from work, collapsed on the sofa, and passed out. When I woke up on Saturday morning, I realized I needed a full day of doing nothing to reboot my system. I was on the verge of burnout.
So, I decided to visit a spa center.
I went alone because I didn't want to talk to anyone. If I had invited my friends, I would have had to engage in conversations, which would have drained all my energy. So, I kept my plan to myself.
I spent some time in a steam room, then moved to a sauna with dry herbal steam. I swam in a pool and even stepped into a snow room once. Between sauna sessions, I sipped herbal tea.
But what I enjoyed the most was the Japanese bath. There were two hot tubs (one at 45C and the other at 40C) plus a swimming pool with water at 6-8C. First, I sat in the hotter tub for about three minutes, then moved to the second one.
After that, I plunged into the cold water before returning to the hot tub. I repeated this cycle several times. By the end, I felt like I was born again.
