questions: How do we choose gifts?
What do you consider when choosing a gift?
What kind of gifts are popular in your country?
What's the best gift you have ever received?
What gift have you received recently?
Do you like to give expensive gifts?
How often do you buy gifts for other people?
Why do people give gifts?
Have you ever received a gift which you didn't like?
samples: When picking gifts for friends or family, we typically begin by thinking about what they like. For example, if the recipient is into gardening, we might look for a nice plant or gardening tools. It's all about finding something that resonates with their hobbies and preferences.

Well, people in my country really like to give books and handmade gifts as well as home décor presents such as frames, figurines and candles. All these things create comfort and remind the receiver of the giver's love and affection. Many people also give flowers and chocolates, especially as "Thank you" presents and cash as a birthday or wedding gift.

Oh no, I don't. Expensive gifts mean more pressure on my monthly expense, which, in turn, means I will have to refuse from something I really need in order to please another person with something costly. What is more, I don't want to buy anybody's love with material things. I'd better do it with actions.
Oh, I actually do it quite often. I would even say almost every day. Just because I like to show thoughtfulness, love and affection to close people and raise a smile on their faces.

I guess there are a lot of reasons why people do it. For example, to show interest and appreciation, or express gratitude to others. People also give gifts to mark milestones and just bring joy and pleasure to the ones they love.

Oh yeah, it happened to me a while ago. I got a key box from my mate which I didn't like at all as it was big and heavy enough and I just couldn't come up with an idea when and where to use it. And still, I struggled to bring a smile to my face to show gratitude to the giver as any present,/u>, to my mind, is worth a 'thank you'.

questions: Do you think your home is clean and tidy?
What housework do you dislike?
What housework do you like?
Do you often do housework?
Do you have breakfast at home every day?
Do you want to learn how to cook well?
Do you like cooking?
Who usually does the cooking in your home?
samples:
(1) I guess it looks clean most of the time. First of all, I try to keep the main surfaces clean. Plus, there are no stains in shower, tub or sink fixtures. There are no crumbs or dirt on the floor. My sink is always empty and clean - there are never dirty dishes in it. And what's important is that everything has a place and is in the place it belongs. I'd say my home is clean enough for guests to visit unexpectedly.

(2) It's super clean. I clean my house on a regular basis to maintain a healthy living environment 'cause dust is a very common cause for colds, coughs, asthma attacks, breathing and respiratory problems, and various types of allergies. Plus, Ilike when it's clean enough to be prepared for surprise visitors.

(3) Oh, my house is constantly messy no matter how hard I try to keep it clean. The thing is that I have a cat. So everything is covered with my cat's hair, so much that it's like a snowstorm in my house. And I'm constantly finding fur everywhere. No matter how often I vacuum it just keeps coming back. It's like a never-ending battle.

(4) I wish it were, but I just don't have time for a cleaning routine. I work full time, and in the evenings I feel so tired that cleaning is what I want to do least. Plus, I have two kids, and they are messmakers. They throw toys around, play with their arts and crafts materials on the floor, and run around like crazy.

(1) What I hate is vacuuming! I think it's because of the noise and monotonous nature of pushing a vacuum around. It just gets on my nerves and bores me to death. Another reason why I hate doing this chore is that I don't like having to move furniture and reach into all the far corners of my house. Plus, every time I vacuum, dust and pet dander get stirred up into the air and make me sneeze and itch. So it's not only a chore that I dread, but it also causes me physical discomfort.

(2) The chore I hate is washing the dishes. It's one of those things that needs to be done every single day, and it's a big pain 'cause I have a lot of pots and pans to clean. Plus, it takes so long because I have to scrub each dish separately. What makes it worse for me is that my hands are always so dry after I finish. But I just can't get used to using gloves.

(3) What I really hate is doing the dishes. So I just say to myself that I will do them tomorrow and just let them pile up. But as you know 'tomorrow never comes'. And the longer I procrastinate, the harder it is to make myself do the chore.
As a result, every day, they slowly accumulate... Lots of plates covered in sauces and crumbs, bowls with a layer of sticky who-knows-what, forks, knives, and spoons all gummed with bits of this and that.

(1) It may sound weird, but I love washing the dishes. It's one of my favorite chores! First of all, doing repetitive motions is calming. I would even say it's therapeutic to me. And I normally use this time to practice mindfulness. I mean, I try to focus on the task at hand, and it helps me clear my mind and relax. Plus, I enjoy listening to the soft sounds of the water running and the gentle clinking of dishes against each other as I wash them. It's like a mini-meditation session for me.

(2) My favourite chore is washing the dishes. First of all, it's a great way to show my family how much I care about them and our home. Plus, when it's all done, I get that feeling of accomplishment and satisfaction when I look at sparkling clean dishes in a freshly wiped sink. And it can be fun. Sometimes I sing along to my favorite songs while washing the dishes and it makes the chore seem less tedious. Sometimes I listen to podcasts and audiobooks. So it can be educational as well.

(3) What I really enjoy is washing the dishes although most people consider it to be a mundane task. But for me, it's like a mini-mediation session. One of the best parts about it is the sound of running water and clinking dishes. The sound of running water creates background noise that blocks out other distractions. The sound of clinking dishes, on the other hand, helps create a calming atmosphere. And I can use this time to focus on my thoughts and feelings without any distractions from other people or technology

No, I don't always have breakfast at home. Sometimes I'm in a rush and I'll grab something quick on the go, like a granola bar or a piece of fruit. Other times, I'll stop at a cafe and get something more substantial, like a breakfast sandwich or a bowl of oatmeal. It just depends on my schedule and what I'm in the mood for

(1) Yeah, I'd love to. If I learn to cook like a pro, I will be able to experiment with different flavors, ingredients, and cooking techniques to create dishes that are truly unique and tailored specifically towards my tastes and preferences.
But, in my opinion, learning how to cook well isn't just about making delicious dishes it's also about eating healthier meals made with fresh ingredients 'cause I will know exactly what ingredients I'm using and how much of each one. Plus, it can save me quite a bit of money 'cause home-cooked meals can be a lot cheaper than buying food at restaurants or getting take out.

(2) Well, cooking is not my thing 'cause it takes too much time and effort. I mean, why bother when there are so many delicious options out there? Stores are filled with readymade meals that are just as tasty. And I can go to a cafe or restaurant whenever I want to. Plus, I don't think I have the patience or skill to cook complicated dishes. And it's not like it's necessary for survival or anything. There are just too many other things that I'd rather do with my time.

Oh yes, I adore it. Cooking at home is always a fun time with my family 'cause we like to cook together. It also lets me control my family's health. What's more, it lets me save money as I have a choice about where and how many products to buy. One more thing I can add is that homemade food tastes much better, especially when I see happy faces of my beloved ones enjoying the meal.

Well, I am the one who always cooks in my home. I do it because I adore cooking and because I am really good at it.
I can easily make a great meal out of random fridge ingredients, and it makes life easy for all my family members. One more reason why I cook for everyone is the fact that I have enough time for that. Though, from time to time my husband and kids help me in the kitchen but not more often than once a week, to my regret.

part2.topic: Place with a lot of trees
part2.cue: Describe a place with a lot of trees that you would like to visit (for example, forest, oasis).
points: what park it is and where it is
why you want to go there
part2.sample:
If I could visit any place with a lot of trees, I would choose Central Park in New York. It's one of the most famous parks in the world, and I've seen it so many times in American movies.
Every time I watch a film set in New York, there's always a scene in Central Park. People are jogging, walking their dogs, or just relaxing on the grass. And then there are those bloggers who show off their amazing apartments with a view of the park. It looks so impressive.
The park is absolutely huge. When I see pictures of it from above, I can't believe how big it is. A giant green space in the middle of a city full of skyscrapers. It's crazy. I'm not an expert on trees, but I think there are a lot of oak, maple, and elm trees there. Some of them have massive trunks, which makes me think the park has been there forever. I can picture myself walking under those tall trees, with the leaves rustling in the wind. You know, it would feel like a little forest in the middle of the city.
Maybe when I finally get there, it won't be as incredible as I imagine. But I still want to see it with my own eyes.

questions: What apps have you used recently?
What apps are you usually interested in?
What apps would you like to use in the future?
How much time do you spend on these apps?
samples: Well, I think all possible kinds. I have a couple of news apps because it's important for me to keep up with current events and know what is happening in my city, country and in the world. I also have a few games just to relax and get my mind off troubles or pass the time while waiting for somebody or queuing. As I am a business person I have to have some apps for business too, for example, email apps, apps for editing documents, reminders, notepad apps, a currency converter and a calculator to be able to do my work wherever I am, even on the go. Oh, I almost forgot to name a weather app, a photo editor, an alarm clock, some trip planners, a few social networks, some music and video apps. Yeah, that's it. Pretty much stuff, actually What is more, I can organize travel information, manage my business and even track my spending habits. I guess this is what explains why I spend that much time on applications.

Well, sometimes it seems to me that I spend around 80% of my free time on them and it frightens me a lot because I almost don't have any time left for active rest with friends and family members. What's worse is I don't do anything to change the situation because the more I use apps, the less I want to stop using them. Apps open so many opportunities and let me do so much stuff just with the help of my phone. I can do shopping, swap messages with friends, listen to music and even watch some film or video on my phone.

questions: Do you mind noises?
Do any noises bother you?
Do you think there's too much noise in modern society?
Are cities becoming noisier?
Where is there louder noise, in cities or in the countryside?
What type of noise do you come across in your daily life?
Are there any sounds that you like?
samples: I would say I'm pretty tolerant to noises when I'm not asleep as I've learned to cut out the unwanted ones. But when I am about to fall asleep, I become very sensitive to any kind of noise, and nearly anything can make me irritated Sometimes I toss and turn throughout the night just because I hear the muffled sound of slammed doors in the flat next door.

There's no worse noise than scraping chalk on a blackboard. You know, many cafes still use such boards as an advertising medium. When I see them, I can't help imagining the way this information was written down. And even the thought of it makes me feel sick.

Yeah, the level of noise is getting higher and higher. In fact, it is so high that it is now regarded a type of environmental pollution. This is because nowadays cities are more crowded than in the past, which means that there's much more traffic on roads. There are more people talking everywhere. Oh, and I nearly forgot to mention air conditioning equipment which is one of the biggest parts of all ambient noise in today's cities.

We are surrounded by different sounds both indoors and outdoors. My typical day starts with the sound of boiling water as I can't imagine my morning without a cup of coffee. Every single day I'm accompanied by roaring engines, slammed doors, mouse clicking and constantly ringing phones

Oh yeah! Splashing waves and screams of sea-gulls sound like music to me. I also enjoy the sound of rain when I'm inside and don't have to go anywhere. And I can't help mentioning the train tracks clanking in a constant pattern This sound makes me fall asleep as soon as the train leaves

part2.cue: Describe an occasion when you heard a stranger speaking on the phone in public.
points: what you were doing at that time
part2.sample:
I don't mind people speaking on the phone in public places only when they have to discuss something that can't wait, and only if they do it quietly and briefly. And I can't stand when people start spilling personal information in the presence of complete strangers.
Several days ago this was just the case. I was standing in the checkout line at the supermarket. The line was long and slow-moving. So I decided to use this time to catch up on my emails. However, that wasn't going to happen 'cause the woman behind me in line received a call.
She was having a long, loud, animated conversation on her cell phone. And she didn't care that a dozen people must have wanted to do what they were planning to. Instead, everyone learned that her mother had diabetes, her boss was cheating on his wife, and her sister was thinking of breaking up with her boyfriend. And she wasn't even afraid that the wrong third party could overhear the conversation.
I was really annoyed. It was an invasion of my personal space and peace of mind. If I could have predicted all that, I would have picked another line. But it was what it was. I was just standing there, hoping this nightmare wouldn't last forever.

questions: What's the colour you dislike?
Have you ever bought something because of its colour?
What is your favourite colour?
What is the most popular colour in your country?
What colours do your friends like most?
What colour would you never use in your home?
samples: I'm not a big fan of white for a few reasons. First, it gets dirty too easily, and it's hard to keep clean, which can be annoying. Also, in my culture, white is linked to funerals and mourning, so it doesn't feel very cheerful. When it comes to home decoration, having too much white reminds me of a hospital, and it doesn't feel cozy at all. That's why I prefer warmer, more inviting colors.

(1) Yes, I bought a canary yellow bag because everyone said it was the trendiest color. I knew right off the bat I wouldn't use it because I don't really like bright colors, but I still bought it. Now it just sits in my closet.

(2) Yes, I bought a silver dress for a party once. Everyone had to wear silver, so I had no choice. I don't really like silver, but I still bought it. After the party, I never wore it again.

(3) Yes, I saw deep teal leather pumps and bought them. I loved the color, but now I don't wear them because I don't have any clothes that match this color.

(4) Yes, I bought a mint green cushion for my sofa. My living room has some pale green curtains, and I wanted the colors to match. I think it really made the room look better

It is yellow that I like as it seems to exude nothing but warmth and happiness. This is the only colour that makes me feel energetic and elated. I think this is the best colour to signify positive emotions.

(1) I would avoid stimulating colours, for instance, large splashes of red and yellow or sharp contrasting colours such as black and white. This is because my bedroom should be a place of peace and tranquility rather than a stimulating environment.

(2) I would advise against too much black as it will make me feel on the low side or even depressed. Similarly, I would try to avoid red because I will never have deep sleep or possibly have trouble falling asleep as it is not an easy bedroom colour to relax.

questions: Have you ever borrowed books from others?
Have you ever borrowed money from others?
Do you like to lend things to others?
How do you feel when people don't return things they borrowed from you?
samples:
(1) Well, plenty of times, actually. I adore reading but, regrettably, can't afford to buy every single book I want to read. So, borrowing books is a great chance for me not to let my reading habits be dictated by my budget.

(2) No, I've never done it as, first of all, I don't have enough time even for reading the books I have, and secondly, as I don't want to cut ties with the person I borrowed a book from in case I either lose or tear it apart.
Oh no, I don't. Lending things always makes me stressed and nervous as I have a fear that other people may damage them, which will make me upset and sour our relations.
Well, I usually feel annoyed and dispirited in such situations as I hate when people break their promises or disappoint my expectations.

part2.cue: Describe a kind of foreign food you like and you have tried.
part2.sample:
Last year while I was on holiday in Greece, I decided to try oysters for the first time. I really wanted to taste them as there were so many people who loved them and the same number of people who hated them. So, on the one hand, I wanted to form my own opinion on this type of seafood. On the other, I was a bit afraid. The place we stayed in was right by the sea, so my friends persuaded me this was the best opportunity to duly appreciate the taste of oysters as they were supposed to be really fresh there. We went to a seafood restaurant and ordered a large plate of oysters. Although they were expensive, I thought there wouldn't be a better chance in the near future, so I was determined to taste them come what may.
My friends started eating, saying every other second how delicious they were. I plucked up my courage, took the first oyster and slurped it before I changed my mind. When my mouth was filled with slime, I had to swallow this slippery liquid just because there were many people around. But if I had been at home, I would have spitted it out immediately as the texture was just horrible.
A few minutes later I thought, okay, one more try. I grabbed another one, not expecting much, but somehow, it actually tasted good. Then I had a third. And before I knew it, I'd basically eaten the whole plate. Now, Now, anytime I get the chance, I order oysters without a second thought.

Sometimes I like wearing hats for practical reasons, you know, as a cover-up for bad-hair days. But in the winter, I hate hats as it's absolutely impossible to take them off without messing up a hairdo.

(2) Not really. Not that I'm timid, but I don't like to be in the centre of everybody's attention, which is inevitable when you're surrounded by non-hatted people wherever you are. So I prefer to go bareheaded.

(1) Well, just my old knitted hat which I wear in the winter to keep my head from cold. And, of course, some cap to prevent a heat stroke in the summer. I never buy expensive hats as when I take them off somewhere inside, I quickly forget about them, so I often have to buy new ones, therefore I care neither about their quality nor the style.

(2) I'm a real hat person, so I have a number of hats that come in a variety of shapes and sizes. My favourite type is a fedora hat as it has some magic power to transform any outfit. I always put it onwhen I need to look respectable. I also have a nice flat cap which makes me look incredibly stylish. (1) Like everything I have, I prefer buying hats and caps online First of all, I can find goods at reasonable prices as everyone knows Internet prices are hard to beat. Another reason is that I can shop anytime. Taking into account the fact that I work long hours, if it weren't for an opportunity to buy clothes and hats online, I would go everywhere naked.

(2) Anywhere, except the Internet. I may buy hats in department stores and even at secondhand stores provided I can try them on. For me, the hat has always been as special an accessory as sunglasses, so I always choose them really carefully.

part2.cue: Describe an interesting activity your friend has done, but you haven't and you want to try.
points: why do you want to try it
part2.sample:
Since my last vacation I've had an overwhelming desire to try flyboarding. As the name suggests, it's like flying on water pressure. You stand on a board which is connected to a watercraft by means of a very long hose. The watercraft gives the flyboard propulsion, so you can move underwater and fly over the water.
First, I saw a video on Facebook which really impressed me.
Then I was on holiday last summer and my friend suggested trying this activity. Of course, I agreed without hesitation, but later understood that I wasn't a suitable candidate for this activity. So I refused. The main reason is that I didn't want to get injured and spend several months in hospital just because I wanted to jump out of water like a dolphin for 15 minutes. And at the time I wasn't fit enough. This meant I wouldn't be able to control my body and movements. I was afraid to damage my spine chord and break bones. However, my biggest fear was to have a heavy blow to the head. I saw that people fell down 100 times before they were able to flyboard properly. Also, it was quite expensive for me. It cost more than 100 dollars per 15 or 20 minutes. If I'd spent so much money, I would have spent the rest of my holiday dying of hunger. So I refused, but my friend didn't. And It looked really impressive. On returning home, I decided to go to the gym regularly to get fitter and try flyboarding next time as it's absolutely different from all the activities I've done to date.
Now I'm looking forward to my next summer holidays as I'm sure it's a lot of fun flying above the water like Superman, let alone the thrill of getting the adrenaline pumping through my body. Also, I wonder whether I will be capable of mastering it and whether it's as difficult as it seems.

What do you consider when choosing a gift?

Why do people give gifts?

samples: When picking gifts for friends or family, we typically begin by thinking about what they like. For example, if the recipient is into gardening, we might look for a nice plant or gardening tools. It's all about finding something that resonates with their hobbies and preferences.

Well, people in my country really like to give books and handmade gifts as well as home décor presents such as frames, figurines and candles. All these things create comfort and remind the receiver of the giver's love and affection. Many people also give flowers and chocolates, especially as "Thank you" presents and cash as a birthday or wedding gift.

Expensive gifts mean more pressure on my monthly expense, which, in turn, means I will have to refuse from something I really need in order to please another person with something costly. What is more, I don't want to buy anybody's love with material things. I'd better do it with actions.
Oh, I actually do it quite often. I would even say almost every day. Just because I like to show thoughtfulness, love and affection to close people and raise a smile on their faces.

I guess there are a lot of reasons why people do it. For example, to show interest and appreciation, or express gratitude to others. People also give gifts to mark milestones and just bring joy and pleasure to the ones they love.

Oh yeah, it happened to me a while ago. I got a key box from my mate which I didn't like at all as it was big and heavy enough and I just couldn't come up with an idea when and where to use it. questions: Do you think your home is clean and tidy?
What housework do you dislike?
What housework do you like?
Do you often do housework?
Do you have breakfast at home every day?
Do you want to learn how to cook well?
Do you like cooking?
Who usually does the cooking in your home?
samples:
(1) I guess it looks clean most of the time. First of all, I try to keep the main surfaces clean. Plus, there are no stains in shower, tub or sink fixtures. There are no crumbs or dirt on the floor. My sink is always empty and clean - there are never dirty dishes in it. And what's important is that everything has a place and is in the place it belongs. I'd say my home is clean enough for guests to visit unexpectedly.

(2) It's super clean. I clean my house on a regular basis to maintain a healthy living environment 'cause dust is a very common cause for colds, coughs, asthma attacks, breathing and respiratory problems, and various types of allergies. Plus, Ilike when it's clean enough to be prepared for surprise visitors.

(3) Oh, my house is constantly messy no matter how hard I try to keep it clean. The thing is that I have a cat. So everything is covered with my cat's hair, so much that it's like a snowstorm in my house. And I'm constantly finding fur everywhere. No matter how often I vacuum it just keeps coming back. It's like a never-ending battle.

(4) I wish it were, but I just don't have time for a cleaning routine. I work full time, and in the evenings I feel so tired that cleaning is what I want to do least. Plus, I have two kids, and they are messmakers. They throw toys around, play with their arts and crafts materials on the floor, and run around like crazy.

(1) What I hate is vacuuming! I think it's because of the noise and monotonous nature of pushing a vacuum around. It just gets on my nerves and bores me to death. Another reason why I hate doing this chore is that I don't like having to move furniture and reach into all the far corners of my house. Plus, every time I vacuum, dust and pet dander get stirred up into the air and make me sneeze and itch. So it's not only a chore that I dread, but it also causes me physical discomfort.

(2) The chore I hate is washing the dishes. It's one of those things that needs to be done every single day, and it's a big pain 'cause I have a lot of pots and pans to clean. Plus, it takes so long because I have to scrub each dish separately. What makes it worse for me is that my hands are always so dry after I finish. But I just can't get used to using gloves.

(3) What I really hate is doing the dishes. So I just say to myself that I will do them tomorrow and just let them pile up. But as you know 'tomorrow never comes'. And the longer I procrastinate, the harder it is to make myself do the chore.
As a result, every day, they slowly accumulate... Lots of plates covered in sauces and crumbs, bowls with a layer of sticky who-knows-what, forks, knives, and spoons all gummed with bits of this and that.

(1) It may sound weird, but I love washing the dishes. It's one of my favorite chores! First of all, doing repetitive motions is calming. I would even say it's therapeutic to me. And I normally use this time to practice mindfulness. I mean, I try to focus on the task at hand, and it helps me clear my mind and relax. Plus, I enjoy listening to the soft sounds of the water running and the gentle clinking of dishes against each other as I wash them. It's like a mini-meditation session for me.

(2) My favourite chore is washing the dishes. First of all, it's a great way to show my family how much I care about them and our home. Plus, when it's all done, I get that feeling of accomplishment and satisfaction when I look at sparkling clean dishes in a freshly wiped sink. And it can be fun. Sometimes I sing along to my favorite songs while washing the dishes and it makes the chore seem less tedious. Sometimes I listen to podcasts and audiobooks. So it can be educational as well.

(3) What I really enjoy is washing the dishes although most people consider it to be a mundane task. But for me, it's like a mini-mediation session. One of the best parts about it is the sound of running water and clinking dishes. The sound of running water creates background noise that blocks out other distractions. The sound of clinking dishes, on the other hand, helps create a calming atmosphere. And I can use this time to focus on my thoughts and feelings without any distractions from other people or technology

No, I don't always have breakfast at home. Sometimes I'm in a rush and I'll grab something quick on the go, like a granola bar or a piece of fruit. Other times, I'll stop at a cafe and get something more substantial, like a breakfast sandwich or a bowl of oatmeal. It just depends on my schedule and what I'm in the mood for

(1) Yeah, I'd love to. If I learn to cook like a pro, I will be able to experiment with different flavors, ingredients, and cooking techniques to create dishes that are truly unique and tailored specifically towards my tastes and preferences.
But, in my opinion, learning how to cook well isn't just about making delicious dishes it's also about eating healthier meals made with fresh ingredients 'cause I will know exactly what ingredients I'm using and how much of each one. Plus, it can save me quite a bit of money 'cause home-cooked meals can be a lot cheaper than buying food at restaurants or getting take out.

(2) Well, cooking is not my thing 'cause it takes too much time and effort. I mean, why bother when there are so many delicious options out there? Stores are filled with readymade meals that are just as tasty. And I can go to a cafe or restaurant whenever I want to. Plus, I don't think I have the patience or skill to cook complicated dishes. And it's not like it's necessary for survival or anything. There are just too many other things that I'd rather do with my time.

Oh yes, I adore it. Cooking at home is always a fun time with my family 'cause we like to cook together. It also lets me control my family's health. What's more, it lets me save money as I have a choice about where and how many products to buy. One more thing I can add is that homemade food tastes much better, especially when I see happy faces of my beloved ones enjoying the meal.

Well, I am the one who always cooks in my home. I do it because I adore cooking and because I am really good at it.
I can easily make a great meal out of random fridge ingredients, and it makes life easy for all my family members. One more reason why I cook for everyone is the fact that I have enough time for that. Though, from time to time my husband and kids help me in the kitchen but not more often than once a week, to my regret.

part2.cue: Describe an unforgettable experience you had.
points: why you think it was unusual
part2.sample:
One of the best experiences I had ever had was participating in one of those 'escape the room' games, you know, where a team of people is locked in a room and must find clues and solve puzzles to complete a given mission and find the key to escape. I had heard a lot about this type of entertainment and really wanted to participate, but only managed to when my friend decided to have an unusual birthday outing.
So, there were 6 or 7 of us in a team. We were kind of spies who broke into someone's house to find some secret files.
Frankly speaking, I don't remember the storyline in detail, but I remember that we had one hour to escape the room to avoid being caught and imprisoned.
The room, in which we were locked, was packed with different stuff such as books, maps, fedoras, magnets, sticky notes, watches, old wigs, compasses, lamps, board games, playing cards. The puzzles were really challenging and intriguing. It was real fun. We were frantically searching for clues.
Some of them involved solving riddles, putting items in the correct order, or finding a set of objects hidden in the room.
What I will never forget is that there was a broken clock and for a long time we couldn't figure out that we had to pay attention to the time it stopped on. By the way, it appeared to be the last clue. So we even thought we would sink with the ship, but then one us had a brainwave and we survived in the last minute.
It was really unusual an activity for all of us as we hadn't done anything like that before. And to tell the truth, I didn't expect it to be so interesting.

samples: I'm not a big fan of white for a few reasons. First, it gets dirty too easily, and it's hard to keep clean, which can be annoying. part2.cue: Describe a time when you were surprised to meet a friend.
points: why you were surprised to meet him or her
part2.sample:
I've got a school friend, but we lost touch when we finished school. And I should say we used to be really good friends, that's why I regretted falling out of contact with him. Recently I decided to call him and invite him to go somewhere so that we can catch up with each other. He seemed to be glad to hear me. So we arranged a meeting at the restaurant the next day at 6 pm.
Then on the day when we were supposed to meet, at the very last minute, he called me and said, 'Let's cancel, I can't make it. I have a fever and sore throat.' He said he had to stay in bed for a week or so. I said, 'It's ok. Get well soon'.
You know, it's a normal situation. People get sick all the time.
But I had already booked a table, and it was too late to cancel a reservation. So I decided to go there anyway.
When I came, I just froze, you know, 'cause I saw my friend talking to some girl. It looked like they had a date. And he obviously didn't look sick at all. What's more, he didn't look embarrassed. I was shocked.

part2.cue: Describe something interesting that you and your friend have discovered.
part2.sample:
You know, one really interesting thing my best friend and I discovered recently is the whole idea of karma. We've always loved deep talks. Like, we can start chatting about something random and end up discussing the meaning of life. So one day, we found this online course about karma and thought, 'Why not try it?'
It turned out to be super cool. The course explained that everything you do has some kind of effect, and even small actions can come back to you later, in good or bad ways. It really made us think differently about a lot of things. Now, whenever something good or bad happens, we kind of sit down and go, 'Okay, what could've caused this? What did we do that maybe led to this?' It really makes us reflect on our behavior. What I really enjoy about learning about karma with my friend is how much it's brought us closer. It's not the kind of thing you can talk about with just anyone. Most people would probably think you're a bit strange if you start discussing karma, energy, or anything spiritual. They might not say it, but you can see it on their face. But with my friend, it's completely different. We can talk about these things without feeling judged, and that's what makes it so special. Honestly, it feels like we're learning and growing together, and that makes the whole experience feel so much more meaningful. I think that's what makes our friendship so great. We're constantly discovering new things together, and that brings us even closer.

part2.cue: Describe a famous person you'd like to meet.

why you'd like to meet this person
part2.sample:
A famous person I'm dying to meet is Volodymyr Zelensky.
He's honestly one of the most inspiring people in the world right now. I've been following his story for a while, and what really amazes me is how he went from being a comedian to becoming the president of Ukraine... and not just any president, but one who ended up leading his country during a full-scale war.
I first saw him in that show Servant of the People - it's actually on Netflix, by the way. It was such a clever idea: a regular school teacher suddenly becomes president. At the time, it felt like pure comedy, but now it almost feels like a documentary. The fact that he played that role and then actually became president... it's just surreal. These days, he's everywhere making speeches, visiting soldiers, and working with leaders around the world. But even with all the pressure and global attention, he still comes across as real and grounded. You can tell he's not just putting on a show. He's really carrying the weight of what's happening.
If I ever got the chance to meet him, I'd love it to be somewhere quiet in Kyiv... just a small café, nothing formal.
I'd want to ask him how he finds the strength to keep going, how he makes tough decisions, and whether he ever misses his old life, the simpler one.
To me, he's not just a leader. He's a symbol of courage and resilience. And that's exactly why I'm dying to meet him
